MaplairMap extends Evented

The central class of the API — it is used to create a map on a page and manipulate it.

Panes

Panes are DOM elements used to control the ordering of layers on the map. You can access panes with map.getPane or map.getPanes methods. New panes can be created with the map.createPane method.

Every map has the following default panes that differ only in zIndex.

Pane zIndex Description
mapPane 'auto' Pane that contains all other map panes
tilePane 200 Pane for GridLayers and TileLayers
overlayPane 400 Pane for vectors (Paths, like Polylines and Polygons), ImageOverlays and VideoOverlays
shadowPane 500 Pane for overlay shadows (e.g. Marker shadows)
markerPane 600 Pane for Icons of Markers
tooltipPane 650 Pane for Tooltips
popupPane 700 Pane for Popups

Map state change events

The map state change events movestart, move, moveend, zoomstart, zoom, zoomend and zoomanim caused by the user (e.g. dragging, scrolling, pinching, pressing a key or clicking a zoom button) have an originalEvent property with the DOM event that started the change. It is undefined for changes made by code (e.g. setView()), which allows to tell them apart, e.g. to avoid feedback loops when synchronizing the view.

Usage example

// initialize the map on the "map" div with a given center and zoom
const map = new MaplairMap('map', {
	center: [51.505, -0.09],
	zoom: 13
});

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new MaplairMap(id: string | HTMLElement, options?: MaplairMapOptions)

Instantiates a map object given the DOM ID of a <div> element or the element itself, and optionally an object literal with MaplairMap options.

id
The <div> element or its DOM ID.

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
crsCRSEPSG3857

The Coordinate Reference System to use. Don't change this if you're not sure what it means.

centerLatLngExpression

Initial geographic center of the map.

zoomnumber

Initial map zoom level.

minZoomnumber

Minimum zoom level of the map. If not specified and at least one GridLayer or TileLayer is in the map, the lowest of their minZoom options will be used instead.

maxZoomnumber

Maximum zoom level of the map. If not specified and at least one GridLayer or TileLayer is in the map, the highest of their maxZoom options will be used instead.

layersLayer[][]

Array of layers that will be added to the map initially.

ariaLabelstring

The accessible name of the map, announced by screen readers, 'Map' by default. The map container gets the ARIA role region with this label, unless it already has a role or label. The default is translated, see I18n.

maxBoundsLatLngBoundsExpression

When this option is set, the map restricts the view to the given geographical bounds, bouncing the user back if the user tries to pan outside the view. To set the restriction dynamically, use setMaxBounds method.

rendererRenderer

The default method for drawing vector layers on the map. SVG or Canvas by default depending on browser support.

zoomAnimationbooleantrue

Whether the map zoom animation is enabled.

zoomAnimationThresholdnumber4

Won't animate zoom if the zoom difference exceeds this value (or 1 if the user prefers reduced motion and animate: true isn't passed).

continuousZoombooleanfalse

Whether zoom animations (e.g. of the zoom control, double click and keyboard) change the view frame by frame through fractional zoom levels, like flyTo() and pinch zoom, instead of scaling the map with a CSS transition between two zoom levels. Also makes the scroll wheel zoom smoothly with each wheel event (see scrollWheelZoom), snapping to zoomSnap when scrolling ends.

fadeAnimationbooleantrue

Whether the tile and popup fade animation is enabled.

markerZoomAnimationbooleantrue

Whether markers animate their zoom with the zoom animation, if disabled they will disappear for the length of the animation.

markerCullingbooleanfalse

Whether markers far outside of the map view (more than half a view away) are taken off the page until the map is moved closer to them. This reduces the browser's rendering work, and the work of repositioning markers while zooming, when a map has many markers (e.g. several thousands) of which only some are visible at a time.

transform3DLimitnumber8388608

Defines the maximum size of a CSS translation transform (2^23). The default value should not be changed unless a web browser positions layers in the wrong place after doing a large panBy.

zoomSnapnumber1

Forces the map's zoom level to always be a multiple of this, particularly right after a fitBounds() or a pinch-zoom. By default, the zoom level snaps to the nearest integer; lower values (e.g. 0.5 or 0.1) allow for greater granularity. A value of 0 means the zoom level will not be snapped after fitBounds or a pinch-zoom.

zoomDeltanumber1

Controls how much the map's zoom level will change after a zoomIn(), zoomOut(), pressing + or - on the keyboard, or using the zoom controls. Values smaller than 1 (e.g. 0.5) allow for greater granularity.

trackResizebooleantrue

Whether the map automatically handles browser window resize to update itself. A hidden map (with the size 0, e.g. display: none in an inactive tab) keeps its size, view and bounds until it is shown again.

attributionControlbooleantrue

Whether a attribution control is added to the map by default.

fullscreenControlbooleanfalse

Whether a fullscreen control is added to the map by default.

rotateControlbooleanfalse

Whether a rotate control is added to the map by default.

zoomControlbooleantrue

Whether a zoom control is added to the map by default.

closePopupOnClickbooleantrue

Set it to false if you don't want popups to close when user clicks the map.

rendererRenderer

The default method for drawing vector layers on the map. A new SVG renderer by default; pass new Canvas() to draw them on a canvas instead.

bearingnumber0

Initial rotation of the map in degrees: the compass direction pointing up, clockwise from north (e.g. 90 for east up), see setBearing().

Added by the optional module maplair/map-rotation.

pinchRotatebooleanfalse

Whether the map can be rotated by turning two fingers, see setBearing().

Added by the optional module maplair/map-rotation.

boxZoombooleantrue

Whether the map can be zoomed to a rectangular area specified by dragging the pointer while pressing the shift key.

displaceboolean|DisplaceHandlerOptions

Whether to displace overlapping CircleMarkers, either true or an object overriding the options of DisplaceHandler. Needs the DisplaceHandler to be added to the map, see there.

doubleClickZoomboolean|'center'true

Whether the map can be zoomed in by double clicking on it and zoomed out by double clicking while holding shift. If passed 'center', double-click zoom will zoom to the center of the view regardless of where the pointer was.

draggingbooleantrue

Whether the map is draggable with pointer or not.

inertiabooleantrue

If enabled, panning of the map will have an inertia effect where the map builds momentum while dragging and continues moving in the same direction for some time. Feels especially nice on touch devices.

inertiaDecelerationnumber3400

The rate with which the inertial movement slows down, in pixels/second².

inertiaMaxSpeednumber1400

Max speed of the inertial movement, in pixels/second.

easeLinearitynumber0.2

The linearity of the easing of the inertial movement.

worldCopyJumpbooleanfalse

With this option enabled, the map tracks when you pan to another "copy" of the world and seamlessly jumps to the original one so that all overlays like markers and vector layers are still visible. A map with an infinite CRS, such as SimpleCRS, does not jump, as it has no copies of the world.

maxBoundsViscositynumber0.0

If maxBounds is set, this option will control how solid the bounds are when dragging the map around. The default value of 0.0 allows the user to drag outside the bounds at normal speed, higher values will slow down map dragging outside bounds, and 1.0 makes the bounds fully solid, preventing the user from dragging outside the bounds.

keyboardbooleantrue

Makes the map focusable and allows users to navigate the map with keyboard arrows and +/- keys.

keyboardPanDeltanumber80

Amount of pixels to pan when pressing an arrow key.

ariaKeyShortcutsboolean|stringfalse

Sets the aria-keyshortcuts attribute of the map container. ARIA names keys by what they type on a given layout, so true uses the names for a US English layout, which can be wrong for pages in other languages; pass a string to set the value for your audience's layout instead.

pinchZoomboolean|'center'true

Whether the map can be zoomed by touch-dragging with two fingers. If passed 'center', it will zoom to the center of the view regardless of where the touch events (fingers) were. Enabled for touch-capable web browsers.

bounceAtZoomLimitsbooleantrue

Set it to false if you don't want the map to zoom beyond min/max zoom and then bounce back when pinch-zooming.

touchZoomboolean|'center'

Deprecated, use pinchZoom instead.

scrollWheelZoomboolean|'center'|'trackpad'true

Whether the map can be zoomed by using the mouse wheel and by pinching on a touchpad (or using the mouse wheel with the Ctrl key). If passed 'center', it will zoom to the center of the view regardless of where the pointer was. If passed 'trackpad', scrolling (e.g. with two fingers on a touchpad) pans the map instead, while pinching still zooms.

wheelDebounceTimenumber40

Limits the rate at which a wheel can fire (in milliseconds). By default, the user can't zoom via wheel more often than once per 40 ms.

wheelPxPerZoomLevelnumber60

How many scroll pixels (as reported by DomEvent.getWheelDelta) mean a change of one full zoom level. Smaller values will make wheel-zooming faster (and vice versa).

tapDragZoomboolean|'center'true

Whether the map can be zoomed with one finger by tapping once, then touching again and dragging down (zoom in) or up (zoom out). If passed 'center', it will zoom to the center of the view regardless of where the finger was.

tapHoldbooleantrue

Enables simulation of contextmenu event on touch and hold.

tapTolerancenumber15

The max number of pixels a user can shift his finger during touch for it to be considered a valid tap.

Events

EventDataDescription
baselayerchangeLayersControlEventFired when the base layer is changed through the layers control.
overlayaddLayersControlEventFired when an overlay is selected through the layers control.
overlayremoveLayersControlEventFired when an overlay is deselected through the layers control.
searchresultSearchResultEventFired when a result of the search control is selected.
dividermoveDividerMoveEventFired when the divider of a SideBySideControl moves.
timechangeTimeChangeEventFired when the current time of a TimeControl changes.
resizeResizeEventFired when the map is resized.
unloadMaplairEventFired when the map is destroyed with remove method.
viewpreresetMaplairEventFired before the map resets its view (see viewreset).
viewresetMaplairEventFired when the map needs to redraw its content (this usually happens on map zoom or load). Very useful for creating custom overlays.
loadMaplairEventFired when the map is initialized (when its center and zoom are set for the first time).
zoomstartMaplairEventFired when the map zoom is about to change (e.g. before zoom animation).
movestartMaplairEventFired when the view of the map starts changing (e.g. user starts dragging the map).
zoomMaplairEventFired repeatedly during any change in zoom level, including zoom and fly animations.
moveMaplairEventFired repeatedly during any movement of the map, including pan and fly animations.
zoomendMaplairEventFired when the map zoom changed, after any animations.
moveendMaplairEventFired when the center of the map stops changing (e.g. user stopped dragging the map or after non-centered zoom).
idleMaplairEventFired when the map becomes idle: the view is not changing (no dragging, panning or zooming, including their animations) and all layers have finished loading (e.g. the tiles of tile layers, see GridLayer.isLoading()). Useful e.g. for taking screenshots or for tests.
locationerrorMaplairErrorEventFired when geolocation (using the locate method) failed.
locationfoundLocationEventFired when geolocation (using the locate method) went successfully.
clickMaplairPointerEventFired when the user clicks (or taps) the map.
dblclickMaplairPointerEventFired when the user double-clicks (or double-taps) the map.
pointerdownMaplairPointerEventFired when the user pushes the pointer on the map.
pointerupMaplairPointerEventFired when the user releases the pointer on the map.
pointeroverMaplairPointerEventFired when the pointer enters the map.
pointeroutMaplairPointerEventFired when the pointer leaves the map.
pointermoveMaplairPointerEventFired while the pointer moves over the map.
contextmenuMaplairPointerEventFired when the user pushes the right mouse button on the map, prevents default browser context menu from showing if there are listeners on this event. Also fired on mobile when the user holds a single touch for a second (also called long press).
preclickMaplairPointerEventFired before pointer click on the map (sometimes useful when you want something to happen on click before any existing click handlers start running).
keydownMaplairKeyboardEventFired when the user presses a key from the keyboard while the map is focused.
keyupMaplairKeyboardEventFired when the user releases a key from the keyboard while the map is focused.
crschangeCrsChangeEventFired when the CRS of the map changes with setCrs(), before the view is reset.
worldcopyjumpWorldCopyJumpEventFired when worldCopyJump moves the map pane by one or more world widths.
pixelratiochangeMaplairEventFired when the devicePixelRatio of the browser changes, e.g. when moving the window to a screen with another resolution or when zooming the page. Tile layers with detectRetina and canvas renderers adapt to it.
zoomanimZoomAnimEventFired at least once per zoom animation. For continuous zoom, like pinch zooming, fired once per frame during zoom.
boxzoomstartMaplairEventFired when the user starts drawing a box to zoom to.
boxzoomendBoxZoomEndEventFired when the user has drawn a box and the map is zoomed to it.
dragstartMaplairEventFired when the user starts dragging the map.
dragMaplairEventFired repeatedly while the user drags the map.
dragendDragEndEventFired when the user stops dragging the map.
focusMaplairEventFired when the map gains focus.
blurMaplairEventFired when the map loses focus.
enterfullscreenMaplairEventFired when the map enters fullscreen.
exitfullscreenMaplairEventFired when the map exits fullscreen.
fullscreenchangeMaplairEventFired when the map enters or exits fullscreen.
layeraddLayerEventFired when a new layer is added to the map.
layerremoveLayerEventFired when some layer is removed from the map.
zoomlevelschangeMaplairEventFired when the number of zoomlevels on the map is changed due to adding or removing a layer.
popupopenPopupEventFired when a popup is opened in the map.
popupclosePopupEventFired when a popup in the map is closed.
autopanstartMaplairEventFired when the map starts autopanning when opening a popup.
tooltipopenTooltipEventFired when a tooltip is opened in the map.
tooltipcloseTooltipEventFired when a tooltip in the map is closed.
rotateMaplairEventFired when the bearing of the map changes, see setBearing(). (maplair/map-rotation)

Methods

Methods for modifying map state

MethodReturnsDescription
setView(center: LatLngExpression, zoom?: number, options?: ZoomPanOptions)this

Sets the view of the map (geographical center and zoom) with the given animation options.

setZoom(zoom: number, options?: ZoomPanOptions)this

Sets the zoom of the map.

zoomIn(delta?: number, options?: ZoomOptions)this

Increases the zoom of the map by delta (zoomDelta by default).

zoomOut(delta?: number, options?: ZoomOptions)this

Decreases the zoom of the map by delta (zoomDelta by default).

setZoomAround(latlng: LatLngExpression | Point, zoom: number, options?: ZoomOptions)this

Zooms the map while keeping a specified geographical point on the map stationary (e.g. used internally for scroll zoom and double-click zoom). Given a Point, it keeps the specified pixel on the map (relative to the top-left corner) stationary instead.

latlng
The geographical point or the pixel offset.
fitBounds(bounds: LatLngBoundsExpression, options?: FitBoundsOptions)this

Sets a map view that contains the given geographical bounds with the maximum zoom level possible.

fitWorld(options?: FitBoundsOptions)this

Sets a map view that mostly contains the whole world with the maximum zoom level possible.

panTo(center: LatLngExpression, options?: PanOptions)this

Pans the map to a given center.

panBy(offset: PointExpression, options?: PanOptions)this

Pans the map by a given number of pixels (animated unless animate: false is passed, or the user prefers reduced motion and the pan is longer than half the map size without animate: true).

flyTo(targetCenter: LatLngExpression, targetZoom?: number, options?: ZoomPanOptions)this

Sets the view of the map (geographical center and zoom) performing a smooth pan-zoom animation. If the user prefers reduced motion (and animate: true isn't passed), it behaves like setView instead, only animating short pans and zooms.

flyToBounds(bounds: LatLngBoundsExpression, options?: FitBoundsOptions)this

Sets the view of the map with a smooth animation like flyTo, but takes a bounds parameter like fitBounds.

setCrs(crs: CRS)this

Changes the Coordinate Reference System of the map, keeping its center and (as far as possible with the zoom levels and zoomSnap) its scale at the center. All layers are redrawn in the new CRS; note that tile layers only work with the CRS their tiles were made for.

setMaxBounds(bounds: LatLngBoundsExpression)this

Restricts the map view to the given bounds (see the maxBounds option).

setMinZoom(zoom: number)this

Sets the lower limit for the available zoom levels (see the minZoom option).

setMaxZoom(zoom: number)this

Sets the upper limit for the available zoom levels (see the maxZoom option).

panInsideBounds(bounds: LatLngBoundsExpression, options?: PanOptions)this

Pans the map to the closest view that would lie inside the given bounds (if it's not already), controlling the animation using the options specific, if any.

panInside(latlng: LatLngExpression, options?: PaddingOptions & PanOptions)this

Pans the map the minimum amount to make the latlng visible. Use padding options to fit the display to more restricted bounds. If latlng is already within the (optionally padded) display bounds, the map will not be panned.

invalidateSize(options?: InvalidateSizeOptions | boolean)this

Checks if the map container size changed and updates the map if so — call it after you've changed the map size dynamically, also animating pan by default. If options.pan is false, panning will not occur. If options.debounceMoveend is true, it will delay moveend event so that it doesn't happen often even if the method is called many times in a row. Passing true instead of options animates the panning.

stop()this

Stops the currently running panTo or flyTo animation, if any.

toggleFullscreen()this

Enters or exits the fullscreen view of the map, see FullscreenControl. Browsers allow entering fullscreen only in response to a user interaction, e.g. a click.

Geolocation methods

MethodReturnsDescription
locate(options?: LocateOptions)this

Tries to locate the user using the Geolocation API, firing a locationfound event with location data on success or a locationerror event on failure, and optionally sets the map view to the user's location with respect to detection accuracy (or to the world view if geolocation failed). Note that, if your page doesn't use HTTPS, this method will fail in modern browsers (Chrome 50 and newer) See LocateOptions for more details.

stopLocate()this

Stops watching location previously initiated by map.locate({watch: true}) and aborts resetting the map view if map.locate was called with {setView: true}.

Methods for getting map state

MethodReturnsDescription
getCenter()LatLng

Returns the geographical center of the map view.

getZoom()number

Returns the current zoom level of the map view.

getBounds()LatLngBounds

Returns the geographical bounds visible in the current map view.

getMinZoom()number

Returns the minimum zoom level of the map (if set in the minZoom option of the map or of any layers), or 0 by default.

getMaxZoom()number

Returns the maximum zoom level of the map (if set in the maxZoom option of the map or of any layers).

getBoundsZoom(bounds: LatLngBoundsExpression, inside?: boolean, padding?: PointExpression)number

Returns the maximum zoom level on which the given bounds fit to the map view in its entirety. If inside (optional) is set to true, the method instead returns the minimum zoom level on which the map view fits into the given bounds in its entirety.

getSize()Point

Returns the current size of the map container (in pixels).

getPixelBounds(center?: LatLngExpression, zoom?: number)Bounds

Returns the bounds of the current map view in projected pixel coordinates (sometimes useful in layer and overlay implementations). If center and zoom is omitted, the map's current zoom level and center is used.

getPixelOrigin()Point

Returns the projected pixel coordinates of the top left point of the map layer (useful in custom layer and overlay implementations).

getPixelWorldBounds(zoom?: number)Bounds | null

Returns the world's bounds in pixel coordinates for zoom level zoom. If zoom is omitted, the map's current zoom level is used.

Returns null for CRSs with infinite bounds.

Conversion methods

MethodReturnsDescription
getZoomScale(toZoom: number, fromZoom?: number)number

Returns the scale factor to be applied to a map transition from zoom level fromZoom to toZoom. Used internally to help with zoom animations.

getScaleZoom(scale: number, fromZoom?: number)number

Returns the zoom level that the map would end up at, if it is at fromZoom level and everything is scaled by a factor of scale. Inverse of getZoomScale.

project(latlng: LatLngExpression, zoom?: number)Point

Projects a geographical coordinate LatLng according to the projection of the map's CRS, then scales it according to zoom and the CRS's Transformation. The result is pixel coordinate relative to the CRS origin.

unproject(point: PointExpression, zoom?: number)LatLng

Inverse of project.

layerPointToLatLng(point: PointExpression)LatLng

Given a pixel coordinate relative to the origin pixel, returns the corresponding geographical coordinate (for the current zoom level).

latLngToLayerPoint(latlng: LatLngExpression)Point

Given a geographical coordinate, returns the corresponding pixel coordinate relative to the origin pixel.

wrapLatLng(latlng: LatLngExpression)LatLng

Returns a LatLng where lat and lng has been wrapped according to the map's CRS's wrapLat and wrapLng properties, if they are outside the CRS's bounds. By default this means longitude is wrapped around the dateline so its value is between -180 and +180 degrees.

wrapLatLngBounds(bounds: LatLngBoundsExpression)LatLngBounds

Returns a LatLngBounds with the same size as the given one, ensuring that its center is within the CRS's bounds. By default this means the center longitude is wrapped around the dateline so its value is between -180 and +180 degrees, and the majority of the bounds overlaps the CRS's bounds.

distance(latlng1: LatLngExpression, latlng2: LatLngExpression)number

Returns the distance between two geographical coordinates according to the map's CRS. By default this measures distance in meters.

containerPointToLayerPoint(point: PointExpression)Point

Given a pixel coordinate relative to the map container, returns the corresponding pixel coordinate relative to the origin pixel.

layerPointToContainerPoint(point: PointExpression)Point

Given a pixel coordinate relative to the origin pixel, returns the corresponding pixel coordinate relative to the map container.

containerPointToLatLng(point: PointExpression)LatLng

Given a pixel coordinate relative to the map container, returns the corresponding geographical coordinate (for the current zoom level).

latLngToContainerPoint(latlng: LatLngExpression)Point

Given a geographical coordinate, returns the corresponding pixel coordinate relative to the map container.

pointerEventToContainerPoint(e: MouseEvent | PointerEvent)Point

Given a PointerEvent object, returns the pixel coordinate relative to the map container where the event took place.

pointerEventToLayerPoint(e: MouseEvent | PointerEvent)Point

Given a PointerEvent object, returns the pixel coordinate relative to the origin pixel where the event took place.

pointerEventToLatLng(e: MouseEvent | PointerEvent)LatLng

Given a PointerEvent object, returns geographical coordinate where the event took place.

Methods for layers and controls

MethodReturnsDescription
addControl(control: Control)this

Adds the given control to the map.

removeControl(control: Control)this

Removes the given control from the map.

addLayer(layer: Layer)this

Adds the given layer to the map.

removeLayer(layer: Layer)this

Removes the given layer from the map.

hasLayer(layer: Layer)boolean

Returns true if the given layer is currently added to the map.

eachLayer(method: (layer: Layer) => void, context?: object)this

Iterates over the layers of the map, optionally specifying context of the iterator function.

map.eachLayer(function(layer){
    layer.bindPopup('Hello');
});
openPopup(popup: Popup | DivOverlayContent, latlng?: LatLngExpression, options?: PopupOptions)this

Opens the specified popup while closing the previously opened (to make sure only one is opened at one time for usability).

Alternatively, creates a popup with the specified content and options and opens it in the given point on a map. String content is rendered as HTML; sanitize untrusted input or pass an HTMLElement with safe textContent instead.

popup
The popup, or the content of a new popup.
closePopup(popup?: Popup, …args: any[])this

Closes the popup previously opened with openPopup (or the given one).

openTooltip(tooltip: Tooltip | DivOverlayContent, latlng?: LatLngExpression, options?: TooltipOptions)this

Opens the specified tooltip.

Alternatively, creates a tooltip with the specified content and options and opens it. String content is rendered as HTML; sanitize untrusted input or pass an HTMLElement with safe textContent instead.

tooltip
The tooltip, or the content of a new tooltip.
closeTooltip(tooltip: Tooltip)this

Closes the tooltip given as parameter.

Map rotation

MethodReturnsDescription
setBearing(bearing: number, options?: { animate?: boolean; })this

Rotates the map around the center of the view, so that the compass direction bearing (in degrees, clockwise from north) points up. Markers, popups and tooltips stay upright. With {animate: true}, the map rotates smoothly (the shorter way round).

Added by the optional module maplair/map-rotation.

getBearing()number

Returns the rotation of the map, see setBearing().

Added by the optional module maplair/map-rotation.

Other methods

MethodReturnsDescription
addHandler(name: string, HandlerClass: new (map: MaplairMap) => Handler)this

Adds a new Handler to the map, given its name and constructor function.

remove()this

Destroys the map and clears all related event listeners.

createPane(name: string, container?: HTMLElement)HTMLElement

Creates a new map pane with the given name if it doesn't exist already, then returns it. The pane is created as a child of container, or as a child of the main map pane if not set.

getPane(pane: string | HTMLElement)HTMLElement

Returns a map pane, given its name or its HTML element (its identity).

getPanes()Record<string, HTMLElement>

Returns a plain object containing the names of all panes as keys and the panes as values.

getContainer()HTMLElement

Returns the HTML element that contains the map.

fire(type: string, data?: object, propagate?: boolean)this

Fires an event of the specified type, see Evented.fire(). The map state change events caused by the user get an originalEvent property (see the class description).

whenReady(callback: (event: { target: MaplairMap; }) => void, context?: object)this

Runs the given function callback when the map gets initialized with a view (center and zoom) and at least one layer, or immediately if it's already initialized, optionally passing a function context.

isFullscreen()boolean

Returns true if the map is viewed in fullscreen.

on(types: string | Record<string, EventListener>, fn?: EventListener | object, context?: object)this

Adds a listener function (fn) to a particular event type of the object. You can optionally specify the context of the listener (object the this keyword will point to). You can also pass several space-separated types (e.g. 'click dblclick'). Alternatively, adds a set of type/listener pairs, e.g. {click: onClick, pointermove: onPointerMove}, with the context as second argument.

off(types?: string | Record<string, EventListener>, fn?: EventListener | object, context?: object, …args: any[])this

Removes a previously added listener function. If no function is specified, it will remove all the listeners of that particular event from the object. Note that if you passed a custom context to on, you must pass the same context to off in order to remove the listener. Alternatively, removes a set of type/listener pairs. Without arguments, removes all listeners to all events on the object, including implicitly attached events.

listens(type: string, fn?: EventListener | boolean, context?: object, propagate?: boolean)boolean

Returns true if a particular event type has any listeners attached to it (or the given listener function, with the given context). The verification can optionally be propagated, it will return true if parents have the listener attached to it. Called as listens(type, propagate?) or listens(type, fn, context?, propagate?).

once(types: string | Record<string, EventListener>, fn?: EventListener | object, context?: object)this

Behaves as on(…), except the listener will only get fired once and then removed.

addEventParent(obj: Evented)this

Adds an event parent - an Evented that will receive propagated events.

removeEventParent(obj: Evented)this

Removes an event parent, so it will stop receiving propagated events.

Runs the constructor hooks of the given class and of its parent classes, which haven't run yet for this object. Classes call it at the end of their constructor, e.g. this.callInitHooks(MyClass). Without cls, runs the hooks of all classes of this object.

Hash

Keeps the view of the map in the hash of the URL, e.g. #13/47.2692/11.4041 (zoom, latitude, longitude, and the bearing of a rotated map) or as geo URI #geo:47.2692,11.4041?z=13 (see the format option), so that it can be bookmarked and shared. The view is restored from the hash (in either format) when creating the Hash and when the hash changes (e.g. with the back button of the browser).

With the layers option, the hash also keeps the base layer and the overlays shown on the map, e.g. #13/47.2692/11.4041?layers=OSM,Bike%20routes.

With the option mode: 'query', the view is kept in the query string instead, e.g. ?zoom=13&lat=47.2692&lng=11.4041, keeping the other parameters of the app.

Inspired by the leaflet-hash plugin.

Usage example

const map = new MaplairMap('map').setView([47.27, 11.40], 13);
new Hash(map);

// with the layers of a layers control
const baseLayers = {OSM: osm, Topo: topo}, overlays = {'Bike routes': bikes};
new LayersControl(baseLayers, overlays).addTo(map);
new Hash(map, {layers: {...baseLayers, ...overlays}});

// in the query string, e.g. ?q=cafe&zoom=13&lat=47.2692&lng=11.4041
new Hash(map, {mode: 'query'});

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new Hash(map: MaplairMap, options?: HashOptions)

Synchronizes the view of map with the hash of the URL.

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
format'zoom/lat/lng'|'geo''zoom/lat/lng'

The format of the hash: 'zoom/lat/lng' for #13/47.2692/11.4041, or 'geo' for a geo URI with the zoom as parameter z like in Android, #geo:47.2692,11.4041?z=13. The bearing of a rotated map is added as fourth number or parameter bearing.

layersRecord<string, Layer>

The layers to keep in the hash by name, e.g. the base layers and overlays of a LayersControl: the names of those on the map are added as parameter layers, and restoring the hash adds the named layers to the map and removes the others.

mode'hash'|'query''hash'

Where to keep the view: 'hash' for the hash of the URL, or 'query' for the parameters zoom, lat, lng, bearing (of a rotated map) and layers of the query string (the format option is ignored), keeping the other parameters, e.g. ?q=cafe&zoom=13&lat=47.2692&lng=11.4041. The view is restored on navigating in the history of the browser (popstate).

Methods

MethodReturnsDescription
remove()this

Stops synchronizing the view with the hash of the URL.

Static members

MethodReturnsDescription
parse(hash: string)HashView | undefined

Parses a hash like #13/47.2692/11.4041[/30][?layers=A,B] or #geo:47.2692,11.4041[?z=13][&layers=A,B] to an object with the center (LatLng), the zoom (if any), the optional bearing and the names of the layers (if any), or returns undefined for other hashes.

format(map: MaplairMap, format?: "zoom/lat/lng" | "geo", layers?: Record<string, Layer>)string

Returns the hash for the view of the map in the given format (see the options), with as many decimal places of the coordinates as needed for the precision of a pixel, and the names of the given layers on the map.

parseQuery(search: string)HashView | undefined

Parses the parameters zoom, lat, lng, bearing and layers of a query string like ?q=cafe&zoom=13&lat=47.2692&lng=11.4041 like parse(), or returns undefined without lat and lng.

formatQuery(map: MaplairMap, layers?: Record<string, Layer>, search?: string)string

Returns the query string search with the parameters for the view of the map (see format()) instead of the previous ones, keeping the other parameters.

MapSync

Synchronizes the views (center, zoom and bearing) of several maps, e.g. to compare different layers side by side: whenever one of the maps moves (by the user or by code, including animations), the other maps follow.

With the options oneWay and fit: 'bounds', smaller maps can follow a main map showing its bounds, e.g. thumbnails next to it.

Inspired by the Leaflet.Sync plugin.

Usage example

const sync = new MapSync([map1, map2]);
// later
sync.remove();

// a thumbnail showing the bounds of the main map
new MapSync([map, thumbnail], {oneWay: true, fit: 'bounds'});

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new MapSync(maps: MaplairMap[], options?: MapSyncOptions)

Synchronizes the views of the given maps, starting with the view of the first map.

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
bearingbooleantrue

Whether to synchronize the bearing of rotated maps (with the map rotation, see MaplairMap.setBearing()).

oneWaybooleanfalse

Whether only the first map leads and the other maps follow it, without moving the first map when they are moved.

fit'center'|'bounds''center'

How the maps follow: 'center' with the same center and zoom, or 'bounds' with the same center, zoomed so that the bounds of the leading map fit (like fitBounds()), for maps of different sizes.

Methods

MethodReturnsDescription
remove()this

Stops synchronizing the maps.

Marker extends Layer

Marker is used to display clickable/draggable icons on the map. Extends Layer.

In addition to shared layer methods like addTo() and remove() and popup methods like bindPopup() you can also use the methods below.

Usage example

new Marker([50.5, 30.5]).addTo(map);

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new Marker(latlng: LatLngExpression, options?: MarkerOptions)

Instantiates a Marker object given a geographical point and optionally an options object.

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
iconIconnew DefaultIcon()

Icon instance to use for rendering the marker. See Icon documentation for details on how to customize the marker icon. If not specified, a common instance of DefaultIcon is used.

keyboardbooleantrue

Whether the marker can be tabbed to with a keyboard and, if interactive, clicked by pressing Enter or Space.

titlestring''

Text for the browser tooltip that appear on marker hover (no tooltip by default). Useful for accessibility.

altstring'Marker'

Text for the alt attribute of the icon image. Useful for accessibility.

zIndexOffsetnumber0

By default, marker images zIndex is set automatically based on its latitude. Use this option if you want to put the marker on top of all others (or below), specifying a high value like 1000 (or high negative value, respectively).

opacitynumber1

The opacity of the marker.

rotationnumber|nullnull

Rotation of the marker icon in degrees, clockwise, around the icon anchor, e.g. for the heading of a vehicle. A rotated marker, even at 0°, has no shadow, since the shadow of an upright pin looks wrong under a tilted one. null means no rotation.

riseOnHoverbooleanfalse

If true, the marker will get on top of others when you hover the pointer over it.

riseOffsetnumber250

The z-index offset used for the riseOnHover feature.

panestring'markerPane'

Map pane where the markers icon will be added.

shadowPanestring'shadowPane'

Map pane where the markers shadow will be added.

shadowbooleantrue

Whether to show the shadow of the marker's icon. Each shadow is an additional element on the page, so disabling shadows noticeably reduces the browser's rendering work when showing many markers (e.g. several thousands), especially while panning and zooming. To disable shadows for all markers, use Marker.mergeOptions({shadow: false}).

bubblingPointerEventsbooleanfalse

When true, a pointer event on this marker will trigger the same event on the map (unless DomEvent.stopPropagation is used).

autoPanOnFocusbooleantrue

When true, the map will pan whenever the marker is focused (via e.g. pressing tab on the keyboard) to ensure the marker is visible within the map's bounds.

draggablebooleanfalse

Whether the marker is draggable with pointer or not.

autoPanbooleanfalse

Whether to pan the map when dragging this marker near its edge or not.

autoPanPaddingPointExpression[50, 50]

Distance (in pixels to the left/right and to the top/bottom) of the map edge to start panning the map.

autoPanSpeednumber10

Number of pixels the map should pan by.

rotateWithViewbooleanfalse

On a rotated map (see MaplairMap.setBearing()), whether the icon rotates with the map (e.g. for arrows pointing in a geographic direction) instead of staying upright. The rotation of the marker is relative to the screen, or to north with rotateWithView.

Added by the optional module maplair/map-rotation.

Options inherited from InteractiveLayerOptions
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
interactivebooleantrue

If false, the layer will not emit pointer events and will act as a part of the underlying map.

bubblingPointerEventsbooleantrue

When true, a pointer event on this layer will trigger the same event on the map (unless DomEvent.stopPropagation is used).

Options inherited from Layer
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
panestring'overlayPane'

By default the layer will be added to the map's overlay pane (overlayPane). Overriding this option will cause the layer to be placed on another pane by default. Not effective if the renderer option is set (the renderer option will override the pane option).

attributionstring|nullnull

String to be shown in the attribution control, e.g. "© OpenStreetMap contributors". It describes the layer data and is often a legal obligation towards copyright holders and tile providers.

attributionOrdernumber0

The position of the attribution in the attribution control: attributions are sorted by it, then by the order of adding, e.g. 1 keeps a legend last.

Methods

Marker movement

MethodReturnsDescription
moveTo(latlng: LatLngExpression, options?: MarkerMovementOptions)this

Moves the marker smoothly to latlng, see moveAlong().

Added by the optional module maplair/marker-movement.

moveAlong(latlngs: LatLngExpression[], options?: MarkerMovementOptions)this

Moves the marker smoothly along the given points, frame by frame at a constant speed, e.g. to follow a vehicle or to replay a track. Fires move with each frame and moveend at the end. A new movement or stopMoving() stops it; with reduced motion, the marker jumps to the end. Inspired by the Leaflet.MovingMarker and Leaflet.AnimatedMarker plugins.

Added by the optional module maplair/marker-movement.

stopMoving()this

Stops the movement of moveTo() or moveAlong().

Added by the optional module maplair/marker-movement.

isMoving()boolean

Returns true while the marker moves with moveTo() or moveAlong().

Added by the optional module maplair/marker-movement.

Popup extends DivOverlay

Used to open popups in certain places of the map. Use Map.openPopup to open popups while making sure that only one popup is open at one time (recommended for usability), or use Map.addLayer to open as many as you want.

Usage example

If you want to just bind a popup to marker click and then open it, it's really easy:

marker.bindPopup(popupContent).openPopup();

Path overlays like polylines also have a bindPopup method.

A popup can be also standalone:

const popup = new Popup()
	.setLatLng(latlng)
	.setContent('<p>Hello world!<br />This is a nice popup.</p>')
	.openOn(map);

or

const popup = new Popup(latlng, {content: '<p>Hello world!<br />This is a nice popup.</p>'})
	.openOn(map);

Security note. Popup string content is rendered as HTML. If your content may include untrusted input (e.g. data from users or external APIs), sanitize it with a library like DOMPurify, or build a DOM element using textContent to render it as plain text:

const el = document.createElement('div');
el.textContent = untrustedString;
marker.bindPopup(el);

Tooltip extends DivOverlay

Used to display small texts on top of map layers.

Usage example

If you want to just bind a tooltip to marker:

marker.bindTooltip("my tooltip text").openTooltip();

Path overlays like polylines also have a bindTooltip method.

A tooltip can be also standalone:

const tooltip = new Tooltip()
	.setLatLng(latlng)
	.setContent('Hello world!<br />This is a nice tooltip.')
	.addTo(map);

or

const tooltip = new Tooltip(latlng, {content: 'Hello world!<br />This is a nice tooltip.'})
	.addTo(map);

Security note. Tooltip string content is rendered as HTML. If your content may include untrusted input (e.g. data from users or external APIs), sanitize it with a library like DOMPurify, or build a DOM element using textContent to render it as plain text:

const el = document.createElement('div');
el.textContent = untrustedString;
marker.bindTooltip(el);

Note about tooltip offset. Maplair takes two options in consideration for computing tooltip offsetting:

  • the offset Tooltip option: it defaults to [0, 0], and it's specific to one tooltip. Add a positive x offset to move the tooltip to the right, and a positive y offset to move it to the bottom. Negatives will move to the left and top.
  • the tooltipAnchor Icon option: this will only be considered for Marker. You should adapt this value if you use a custom icon.

Direction where to open the tooltip. TileLayer extends GridLayer

Used to load and display tile layers on the map. Note that most tile servers require attribution, which you can set under Layer. Extends GridLayer.

URL template

A string of the following form:

'https://{s}.somedomain.com/blabla/{z}/{x}/{y}{r}.png'

{s} means one of the available subdomains (used sequentially to help with browser parallel requests per domain limitation; subdomain values are specified in options; a, b or c by default, can be omitted), {z} — zoom level, {x} and {y} — tile coordinates. {r} can be used to add "@2x" to the URL to load retina tiles.

You can use custom keys in the template, which will be evaluated from TileLayer options, like this:

new TileLayer('https://{s}.somedomain.com/{foo}/{z}/{x}/{y}.png', {foo: 'bar'});

Layers extending TileLayer might reimplement the getTileUrl() method.

Usage example

new TileLayer('https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?{foo}', {foo: 'bar', attribution: '© <a href="https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright">OpenStreetMap contributors</a>'}).addTo(map);

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
minZoomnumber0

The minimum zoom level down to which this layer will be displayed (inclusive).

maxZoomnumber18

The maximum zoom level up to which this layer will be displayed (inclusive).

subdomainsstring|string[]'abc'

Subdomains of the tile service. Can be passed in the form of one string (where each letter is a subdomain name) or an array of strings.

errorTileUrlstring''

URL to the tile image to show in place of the tile that failed to load.

zoomOffsetnumber0

The zoom number used in tile URLs will be offset with this value.

tmsbooleanfalse

If true, inverses Y axis numbering for tiles (turn this on for TMS services).

zoomReversebooleanfalse

If set to true, the zoom number used in tile URLs will be reversed (maxZoom - zoom instead of zoom).

detectRetinabooleanfalse

If true and user is on a retina display, it will request four tiles of half the specified size and a bigger zoom level in place of one to utilize the high resolution.

crossOriginboolean|stringfalse

Whether the crossOrigin attribute will be added to the tiles. If a String is provided, all tiles will have their crossOrigin attribute set to the String provided. This is needed if you want to access tile pixel data. Refer to CORS Settings for valid String values.

referrerPolicyReferrerPolicy'strict-origin-when-cross-origin'

Sets the tiles' referrerPolicy attribute set to the String provided. See HTMLImageElement.referrerPolicy for possible values.

Tile providers might require you to use a specific referrer policy (e.g. to verify API tokens or prevent abuse). Specifically, if you are using tiles from tile.openstreetmap.org or tile.osm.org, you should not change this value.

fetchOptionsRequestInit|nullnull

If set, the tiles are loaded with fetch() using these options (see RequestInit), e.g. {headers: {Authorization: 'Bearer …'}} for tile servers requiring custom HTTP headers. Requests of tiles that are no longer needed (e.g. after panning or zooming away) are aborted. Cross-origin tile servers have to allow such requests with CORS headers.

Width and height of tiles in the grid. Use a number if width and height are equal, or Point(width, height) otherwise.

opacitynumber1

Opacity of the tiles. Can be used in the createTile() function.

placeholderstring|nullnull

A CSS background shown in place of tiles while they are loading, e.g. '#ddd' or 'url(loading.svg) center no-repeat #eee'. Tiles with a placeholder appear without fading in.

updateWhenIdlebooleanfalse

Load new tiles only when panning ends.

updateWhenZoomingbooleantrue

By default, a smooth zoom animation (during a pinch zoom or a flyTo()) will update grid layers every integer zoom level. Setting this option to false will update the grid layer only when the smooth animation ends.

updateIntervalnumber200

Tiles will not update more than once every updateInterval milliseconds when panning.

zIndexnumber1

The explicit zIndex of the tile layer.

boundsLatLngBoundsExpression|nullnull

If set, tiles will only be loaded inside the set LatLngBounds.

minZoomnumber0

The minimum zoom level down to which this layer will be displayed (inclusive).

maxZoomnumber

The maximum zoom level up to which this layer will be displayed (inclusive).

maxNativeZoomnumber

Maximum zoom number the tile source has available. If it is specified, the tiles on all zoom levels higher than maxNativeZoom will be loaded from maxNativeZoom level and auto-scaled.

minNativeZoomnumber

Minimum zoom number the tile source has available. If it is specified, the tiles on all zoom levels lower than minNativeZoom will be loaded from minNativeZoom level and auto-scaled.

noWrapbooleanfalse

Whether the layer is wrapped around the antimeridian. If true, the GridLayer will only be displayed once at low zoom levels. Has no effect when the map CRS doesn't wrap around. Can be used in combination with bounds to prevent requesting tiles outside the CRS limits.

panestring'tilePane'

Map pane where the grid layer will be added.

classNamestring''

A custom class name to assign to the tile layer. Empty by default.

pixelatedbooleanfalse

Whether to scale the tiles with nearest-neighbour interpolation (image-rendering: pixelated) instead of smoothing them, so that their pixels stay crisp, e.g. while zooming or beyond maxNativeZoom. Useful for raster data, pixel art or scientific imagery.

keepBuffernumber2

When panning the map, keep this many rows and columns of tiles before unloading them.

attributionstring|nullnull

String to be shown in the attribution control, e.g. "© OpenStreetMap contributors". It describes the layer data and is often a legal obligation towards copyright holders and tile providers.

attributionOrdernumber0

The position of the attribution in the attribution control: attributions are sorted by it, then by the order of adding, e.g. 1 keeps a legend last.

WMSTileLayer extends TileLayer

Used to display WMS services as tile layers on the map. Extends TileLayer.

Usage example

const nexrad = new WMSTileLayer("http://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/wms/nexrad/n0r.cgi", {
	layers: 'nexrad-n0r-900913',
	format: 'image/png',
	transparent: true,
	attribution: "Weather data © 2012 IEM Nexrad"
});

ImageOverlay extends Layer

Used to load and display a single image over specific bounds of the map. Extends Layer.

Usage example

const imageUrl = 'https://maps.lib.utexas.edu/maps/historical/newark_nj_1922.jpg',
	imageBounds = [[40.712216, -74.22655], [40.773941, -74.12544]];
new ImageOverlay(imageUrl, imageBounds).addTo(map);

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new ImageOverlay(url: string | HTMLImageElement, bounds: LatLngBoundsExpression, options?: ImageOverlayOptions)

Instantiates an image overlay object given the URL of the image (or an image element) and the geographical bounds it is tied to.

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
opacitynumber1

The opacity of the image overlay.

altstring''

Text for the alt attribute of the image (useful for accessibility).

interactivebooleanfalse

If true, the image overlay will emit pointer events when clicked or hovered.

crossOriginboolean|stringfalse

Whether the crossOrigin attribute will be added to the image. If a String is provided, the image will have its crossOrigin attribute set to the String provided. This is needed if you want to access image pixel data. Refer to CORS Settings for valid String values.

errorOverlayUrlstring''

URL to the overlay image to show in place of the overlay that failed to load.

zIndexnumber1

The explicit zIndex of the overlay layer.

classNamestring''

A custom class name to assign to the image. Empty by default.

pixelatedbooleanfalse

Whether to scale the image with nearest-neighbour interpolation (image-rendering: pixelated) instead of smoothing it, so that its pixels stay crisp when zoomed in. Useful for raster data, pixel art or scientific imagery.

decodingstring'auto'

Tells the browser whether to decode the image in a synchronous fashion, as per the decoding HTML attribute. If the image overlay is flickering when being added/removed, set this option to 'sync'.

Options inherited from InteractiveLayerOptions
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
interactivebooleantrue

If false, the layer will not emit pointer events and will act as a part of the underlying map.

bubblingPointerEventsbooleantrue

When true, a pointer event on this layer will trigger the same event on the map (unless DomEvent.stopPropagation is used).

Options inherited from Layer
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
panestring'overlayPane'

By default the layer will be added to the map's overlay pane (overlayPane). Overriding this option will cause the layer to be placed on another pane by default. Not effective if the renderer option is set (the renderer option will override the pane option).

attributionstring|nullnull

String to be shown in the attribution control, e.g. "© OpenStreetMap contributors". It describes the layer data and is often a legal obligation towards copyright holders and tile providers.

attributionOrdernumber0

The position of the attribution in the attribution control: attributions are sorted by it, then by the order of adding, e.g. 1 keeps a legend last.

Events

EventDataDescription
loadMaplairEventFired when the ImageOverlay layer has loaded its image.
errorMaplairEventFired when the ImageOverlay layer fails to load its image.

EventDataDescription

pointeroutMaplairPointerEventFired when the pointer leaves the layer, if it is interactive.
contextmenuMaplairPointerEventFired when the user right-clicks on the layer, if it is interactive; prevents default browser context menu from showing if there are listeners on this event. Also fired on mobile when the user holds a single touch for a second (also called long press).
popupopenPopupEventFired when a popup bound to this layer is opened.
popupclosePopupEventFired when a popup bound to this layer is closed.
tooltipopenTooltipEventFired when a tooltip bound to this layer is opened.
tooltipcloseTooltipEventFired when a tooltip bound to this layer is closed.

VideoOverlay extends ImageOverlay

Used to load and display a video player over specific bounds of the map. Extends ImageOverlay.

A video overlay uses the <video> HTML element; getElement() returns the instance of HTMLVideoElement used by this overlay.

Usage example

const videoUrl = 'https://www.mapbox.com/bites/00188/patricia_nasa.webm',
	videoBounds = [[ 32, -130], [ 13, -100]];
new VideoOverlay(videoUrl, videoBounds ).addTo(map);

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new VideoOverlay(video: string | string[] | HTMLVideoElement, bounds: LatLngBoundsExpression, options?: VideoOverlayOptions | undefined)

Instantiates a video overlay object given the URL of the video (or array of URLs, or even a video element) and the geographical bounds it is tied to.

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
autoplaybooleantrue

Whether the video starts playing automatically when loaded. On some browsers autoplay will only work with muted: true.

controlsbooleanfalse

Whether the browser will offer controls to allow the user to control video playback, including volume, seeking, and pause/resume playback.

loopbooleantrue

Whether the video will loop back to the beginning when played.

keepAspectRatiobooleantrue

Whether the video will save aspect ratio after the projection.

mutedbooleanfalse

Whether the video starts on mute when loaded.

playsInlinebooleantrue

Mobile browsers will play the video right where it is instead of open it up in fullscreen mode.

SVGOverlay extends ImageOverlay

Used to load, display and provide DOM access to an SVG file over specific bounds of the map. Extends ImageOverlay.

An SVG overlay uses the <svg> element; getElement() returns the instance of SVGElement used by this overlay.

Usage example

const svgElement = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "svg");
svgElement.setAttribute('xmlns', "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg");
svgElement.setAttribute('viewBox', "0 0 200 200");
svgElement.innerHTML = '<rect width="200" height="200"/><rect x="75" y="23" width="50" height="50" style="fill:red"/><rect x="75" y="123" width="50" height="50" style="fill:#0013ff"/>';
const svgElementBounds = [ [ 32, -130 ], [ 13, -100 ] ];
new SVGOverlay(svgElement, svgElementBounds).addTo(map);

ConstructorDescription
new SVGOverlay(svg: SVGElement, bounds: LatLngBoundsExpression, options?: ImageOverlayOptions | undefined)

Instantiates an image overlay object given an SVG element and the geographical bounds it is tied to. A viewBox attribute is required on the SVG element to zoom in and out properly.

on(types: string | Record<string, EventListener>, fn?: EventListener | object, context?: object)this

Adds a listener function (fn) to a particular event type of the object. You can optionally specify the context of the listener (object the this keyword will point to). You can also pass several space-separated types (e.g. 'click dblclick'). Alternatively, adds a set of type/listener pairs, e.g. {click: onClick, pointermove: onPointerMove}, with the context as second argument.

off(types?: string | Record<string, EventListener>, fn?: EventListener | object, context?: object, …args: any[])this

Removes a previously added listener function. If no function is specified, it will remove all the listeners of that particular event from the object. Note that if you passed a custom context to on, you must pass the same context to off in order to remove the listener. Alternatively, removes a set of type/listener pairs. Without arguments, removes all listeners to all events on the object, including implicitly attached events.

fire(type: string, data?: object, propagate?: boolean)this

Fires an event of the specified type. You can optionally provide a data object — the first argument of the listener function will contain its properties. The event can optionally be propagated to event parents.

listens(type: string, fn?: EventListener | boolean, context?: object, propagate?: boolean)boolean

Returns true if a particular event type has any listeners attached to it (or the given listener function, with the given context). The verification can optionally be propagated, it will return true if parents have the listener attached to it. Called as listens(type, propagate?) or listens(type, fn, context?, propagate?).

once(types: string | Record<string, EventListener>, fn?: EventListener | object, context?: object)this

Behaves as on(…), except the listener will only get fired once and then removed.

HeatLayer extends BlanketOverlay

A heatmap of points, each with an optional intensity, drawn on a canvas: the points are drawn as blurred circles adding up, and colored by a gradient. Nearby points are merged into a grid for speed, so that tens of thousands of points stay fast.

Inspired by the Leaflet.heat plugin and its simpleheat algorithm.

Usage example

new HeatLayer([
	[47.27, 11.40, 0.5], // latitude, longitude, intensity
	[47.28, 11.41],
	new LatLng(47.26, 11.39)
], {radius: 20}).addTo(map);

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new HeatLayer(latlngs?: LatLngExpression[], options?: HeatLayerOptions)

Creates a heatmap of the given points: LatLngs or arrays [lat, lng, intensity] (the intensity defaults to 1).

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
radiusnumber25

The radius of each point in pixels.

blurnumber15

The amount of blur in pixels.

maxnumber1

The intensity with the strongest color.

maxZoomnumber

The zoom level where the points reach the full intensity; below it, the intensity is halved per zoom level. By default the maximum zoom of the map.

minOpacitynumber0.05

The minimum opacity of the heat.

gradientRecord<number, string>{0.4: 'blue', 0.6: 'cyan', 0.7: 'lime', 0.8: 'yellow', 1: 'red'}

The colors for the intensities from 0 to 1, any CSS colors.

panestring'overlayPane'

The map pane of the layer.

Options inherited from BlanketOverlay
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
paddingnumber0.1

How much to extend the clip area around the map view (relative to its size) e.g. 0.1 would be 10% of map view in each direction.

continuousbooleanfalse

When false, the blanket will update its position only when the map state settles (after a pan/zoom animation). When true, it will update when the map state changes (during pan/zoom animations).

Options inherited from Layer
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
panestring'overlayPane'

By default the layer will be added to the map's overlay pane (overlayPane). Overriding this option will cause the layer to be placed on another pane by default. Not effective if the renderer option is set (the renderer option will override the pane option).

attributionstring|nullnull

String to be shown in the attribution control, e.g. "© OpenStreetMap contributors". It describes the layer data and is often a legal obligation towards copyright holders and tile providers.

attributionOrdernumber0

The position of the attribution in the attribution control: attributions are sorted by it, then by the order of adding, e.g. 1 keeps a legend last.

Path extends Layer

An abstract class that contains options and constants shared between vector overlays (Polygon, Polyline, Circle). Do not use it directly. Extends Layer.

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
strokebooleantrue

Whether to draw stroke along the path. Set it to false to disable borders on polygons or circles.

colorstring'#3388ff'

Stroke color.

weightnumber3

Stroke width in pixels.

opacitynumber1

Stroke opacity.

lineCapstring'round'

A string that defines shape to be used at the end of the stroke.

lineJoinstring'round'

A string that defines shape to be used at the corners of the stroke.

dashArraystring|nullnull

A string that defines the stroke dash pattern.

dashOffsetstring|nullnull

A string that defines the distance into the dash pattern to start the dash.

fillbooleanfalse

Whether to fill the path with color. Set it to false to disable filling on polygons or circles. The default depends on the class: true for polygons and circles.

fillColorstring|nullnull

Fill color. Defaults to the value of the color option.

fillOpacitynumber0.2

Fill opacity.

fillRulestring'evenodd'

A string that defines how the inside of a shape is determined.

classNamestring

Custom class name set on an element. Only for SVG renderer. Applied when the element is created; setStyle does not update it afterwards.

rendererRenderer

Use this specific instance of Renderer for this path. If not set, the path uses the map's renderer, which is SVG by default. If set, it overrides the pane option.

dashSpeednumber0

Animates the dashes of the dashArray along the path ("marching ants"), e.g. to show the direction of a flow: the speed in pixels per second, negative for the opposite direction. Not animated with reduced motion.

Added by the optional module maplair/dash-animation.

arrowheadsboolean|{size?: number, repeat?: number, color?: string}false

Arrowheads along a polyline: true for one at the end of each line, or an object with the size (in pixels, default 10), repeat (an arrowhead every that many pixels instead) and color (default: the color of the path).

Added by the optional module maplair/path-decorations.

textstring|{content: string, repeat?: boolean, center?: boolean, offset?: number, fontSize?: number, color?: string}|nullnull

Text along a polyline, e.g. a street name: the text, or an object with the content, repeat (repeat the text along the whole line), center (center it on the line), offset (in pixels, perpendicular to the line), fontSize (in pixels, default 12) and color (default: the color of the path).

Added by the optional module maplair/path-decorations.

Polyline extends Path

A class for drawing polyline overlays on a map. Extends Path.

Usage example

// create a red polyline from an array of LatLng points
const latlngs = [
	[45.51, -122.68],
	[37.77, -122.43],
	[34.04, -118.2]
];

const polyline = new Polyline(latlngs, {color: 'red'}).addTo(map);

// zoom the map to the polyline
map.fitBounds(polyline.getBounds());

You can also pass a multi-dimensional array to represent a MultiPolyline shape:

// create a red polyline from an array of arrays of LatLng points
const latlngs = [
	[[45.51, -122.68],
	 [37.77, -122.43],
	 [34.04, -118.2]],
	[[40.78, -73.91],
	 [41.83, -87.62],
	 [32.76, -96.72]]
];

Polygon extends Polyline

A class for drawing polygon overlays on a map. Extends Polyline.

Note that points you pass when creating a polygon shouldn't have an additional last point equal to the first one — it's better to filter out such points.

Usage example

// create a red polygon from an array of LatLng points
const latlngs = [[37, -109.05],[41, -109.03],[41, -102.05],[37, -102.04]];

const polygon = new Polygon(latlngs, {color: 'red'}).addTo(map);

// zoom the map to the polygon
map.fitBounds(polygon.getBounds());

You can also pass an array of arrays of latlngs, with the first array representing the outer shape and the other arrays representing holes in the outer shape:

const latlngs = [
  [[37, -109.05],[41, -109.03],[41, -102.05],[37, -102.04]], // outer ring
  [[37.29, -108.58],[40.71, -108.58],[40.71, -102.50],[37.29, -102.50]] // hole
];

Additionally, you can pass a multi-dimensional array to represent a MultiPolygon shape.

const latlngs = [
  [ // first polygon
    [[37, -109.05],[41, -109.03],[41, -102.05],[37, -102.04]], // outer ring
    [[37.29, -108.58],[40.71, -108.58],[40.71, -102.50],[37.29, -102.50]] // hole
  ],
  [ // second polygon
    [[41, -111.03],[45, -111.04],[45, -104.05],[41, -104.05]]
  ]
];

Rectangle extends Polygon

A class for drawing rectangle overlays on a map. Extends Polygon.

Usage example

// define rectangle geographical bounds
const bounds = [[54.559322, -5.767822], [56.1210604, -3.021240]];

// create an orange rectangle
new Rectangle(bounds, {color: "#ff7800", weight: 1}).addTo(map);

// zoom the map to the rectangle bounds
map.fitBounds(bounds);

ConstructorDescription

Instantiates a rectangle object given the geographical bounds, and an optional options object.

Adds a listener function (fn) to a particular event type of the object. You can optionally specify the context of the listener (object the this keyword will point to). You can also pass several space-separated types (e.g. 'click dblclick'). Alternatively, adds a set of type/listener pairs, e.g. {click: onClick, pointermove: onPointerMove}, with the context as second argument.

off(types?: string | Record<string, EventListener>, fn?: EventListener | object, context?: object, …args: any[])this

Removes a previously added listener function. If no function is specified, it will remove all the listeners of that particular event from the object. Note that if you passed a custom context to on, you must pass the same context to off in order to remove the listener. Alternatively, removes a set of type/listener pairs. Without arguments, removes all listeners to all events on the object, including implicitly attached events.

fire(type: string, data?: object, propagate?: boolean)this

Fires an event of the specified type. You can optionally provide a data object — the first argument of the listener function will contain its properties. The event can optionally be propagated to event parents.

listens(type: string, fn?: EventListener | boolean, context?: object, propagate?: boolean)boolean

Returns true if a particular event type has any listeners attached to it (or the given listener function, with the given context). The verification can optionally be propagated, it will return true if parents have the listener attached to it. Called as listens(type, propagate?) or listens(type, fn, context?, propagate?).

once(types: string | Record<string, EventListener>, fn?: EventListener | object, context?: object)this

Behaves as on(…), except the listener will only get fired once and then removed.

Adds an event parent - an Evented that will receive propagated events.

removeEventParent(obj: Evented)this

Removes an event parent, so it will stop receiving propagated events.

Circle extends CircleMarker

A class for drawing circle overlays on a map with radius specified in meters. Extends CircleMarker, its setRadius() and getRadius() use meters.

It's an approximation and starts to diverge from a real circle closer to poles (due to projection distortion).

Usage example

new Circle([50.5, 30.5], {radius: 200}).addTo(map);

Adds a listener function (fn) to a particular event type of the object. You can optionally specify the context of the listener (object the this keyword will point to). Removes a previously added listener function. If no function is specified, it will remove all the listeners of that particular event from the object. Fires an event of the specified type. You can optionally provide a data object — the first argument of the listener function will contain its properties. The event can optionally be propagated to event parents.

listens(type: string, fn?: EventListener | boolean, context?: object, propagate?: boolean)boolean

Returns true if a particular event type has any listeners attached to it (or the given listener function, with the given context). The verification can optionally be propagated, it will return true if parents have the listener attached to it. Called as listens(type, propagate?) or listens(type, fn, context?, propagate?).

SVG extends Renderer

Allows vector layers to be displayed with SVG. Inherits Renderer.

Usage example

Use SVG by default for all paths in the map:

const map = new MaplairMap('map', {
	renderer: new SVG()
});

Use a SVG renderer with extra padding for specific vector geometries:

const map = new MaplairMap('map');
const myRenderer = new SVG({ padding: 0.5 });
const line = new Polyline( coordinates, { renderer: myRenderer } );
const circle = new Circle( center, { renderer: myRenderer, radius: 100 } );

Canvas extends Renderer

Allows vector layers to be displayed with <canvas>. Inherits Renderer.

Usage example

Use Canvas by default for all paths in the map:

const map = new MaplairMap('map', {
	renderer: new Canvas()
});

Use a Canvas renderer with extra padding for specific vector geometries:

const map = new MaplairMap('map');
const myRenderer = new Canvas({ padding: 0.5 });
const line = new Polyline( coordinates, { renderer: myRenderer } );
const circle =  new Circle( center, { renderer: myRenderer, radius: 100 } );

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new Canvas(options?: CanvasOptions | undefined)

Creates a Canvas renderer with the given options.

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
tolerancenumber0

How much to extend the click tolerance around a path/object on the map.

Options inherited from BlanketOverlay
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
paddingnumber0.1

How much to extend the clip area around the map view (relative to its size) e.g. 0.1 would be 10% of map view in each direction.

continuousbooleanfalse

When false, the blanket will update its position only when the map state settles (after a pan/zoom animation). When true, it will update when the map state changes (during pan/zoom animations).

Options inherited from Layer
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
panestring'overlayPane'

By default the layer will be added to the map's overlay pane (overlayPane). Overriding this option will cause the layer to be placed on another pane by default. Not effective if the renderer option is set (the renderer option will override the pane option).

attributionstring|nullnull

String to be shown in the attribution control, e.g. "© OpenStreetMap contributors". It describes the layer data and is often a legal obligation towards copyright holders and tile providers.

attributionOrdernumber0

The position of the attribution in the attribution control: attributions are sorted by it, then by the order of adding, e.g. 1 keeps a legend last.

LayerGroup extends Layer

Used to group several layers and handle them as one. If you add it to the map, any layers added or removed from the group will be added/removed on the map as well. Extends Layer.

Usage example

new LayerGroup([marker1, marker2])
	.addLayer(polyline)
	.addTo(map);

Creates a layer group, optionally given an initial set of layers and an options object.

FeatureGroup extends LayerGroup

Extended LayerGroup that makes it easier to do the same thing to all its member layers:

  • bindPopup binds a popup to all of the layers at once (likewise with bindTooltip)
  • Events are propagated to the FeatureGroup, so if the group has an event handler, it will handle events from any of the layers. This includes pointer events and custom events.
  • Has layeradd and layerremove events

Usage example

new FeatureGroup([marker1, marker2, polyline])
	.bindPopup('Hello world!')
	.on('click', function() { alert('Clicked on a member of the group!'); })
	.addTo(map);

GeoJSON extends FeatureGroup

Represents a GeoJSON object or an array of GeoJSON objects. Allows you to parse GeoJSON data and display it on the map. Extends FeatureGroup.

There are several static functions which can be called without instantiating GeoJSON.

Usage example

new GeoJSON(data, {
	style: function (feature) {
		return {color: feature.properties.color};
	}
}).bindPopup(function (layer) {
	return layer.feature.properties.description;
}).addTo(map);

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new GeoJSON(geojson?: GeoJSONData | GeoJSONData[] | null, options?: GeoJSONOptions)

Creates a GeoJSON layer. Optionally accepts an object in GeoJSON format to display on the map (you can alternatively add it later with addData method) and an options object.

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
pointToLayer(geoJsonPoint: Feature, latlng: LatLng) => Layer

A Function defining how GeoJSON points spawn Maplair layers. It is internally called when data is added, passing the GeoJSON point feature and its LatLng. The default is to spawn a default Marker:

function(geoJsonPoint, latlng) {
return new Marker(latlng);
}
stylePathOptions|((geoJsonFeature: Feature) => PathOptions)

A Function defining the Path options for styling GeoJSON lines and polygons, called internally when data is added. The default value is to not override any defaults:

function (geoJsonFeature) {
return {}
}
onEachFeature(feature: Feature, layer: Layer) => void

A Function that will be called once for each created Feature, after it has been created and styled. Useful for attaching events and popups to features. It will receive the feature as the first argument and its corresponding spawned layer from asFeature as the second. The default is to do nothing with the newly created layers:

function (feature, layer) {}
filter(geoJsonFeature: Feature) => boolean

A Function that will be used to decide whether to include a feature or not. The default is to include all features:

function (geoJsonFeature) {
return true;
}

Note: dynamically changing the filter option will have effect only on newly added data. It will not re-evaluate already included features.

coordsToLatLng(coords: number[]) => LatLng

A Function that will be used for converting GeoJSON coordinates to LatLngs. The default is the coordsToLatLng static method.

markersInheritOptionsbooleanfalse

Whether default Markers for "Point" type Features inherit from group options.

urlstringundefined

A URL to load the GeoJSON data from when creating the layer.

Added by the optional module maplair/geojson-loading.

fetchOptionsRequestInitundefined

Options for fetch() when loading, e.g. {headers: {Authorization: 'Bearer …'}}.

Added by the optional module maplair/geojson-loading.

fitBoundsbooleanfalse

Whether to fit the map to the bounds of the data once loaded.

Added by the optional module maplair/geojson-loading.

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
interactivebooleantrue

If false, the layer will not emit pointer events and will act as a part of the underlying map.

bubblingPointerEventsbooleantrue

When true, a pointer event on this layer will trigger the same event on the map (unless DomEvent.stopPropagation is used).

Options inherited from Layer
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
panestring'overlayPane'

By default the layer will be added to the map's overlay pane (overlayPane). Overriding this option will cause the layer to be placed on another pane by default. Not effective if the renderer option is set (the renderer option will override the pane option).

attributionstring|nullnull

String to be shown in the attribution control, e.g. "© OpenStreetMap contributors". It describes the layer data and is often a legal obligation towards copyright holders and tile providers.

attributionOrdernumber0

The position of the attribution in the attribution control: attributions are sorted by it, then by the order of adding, e.g. 1 keeps a legend last.

geometryToLayer(geojson: GeoJsonObject, options?: GeoJSONOptions)Layer | null

Creates a LatLng object from an array of 2 numbers (longitude, latitude) or 3 numbers (longitude, latitude, altitude) used in GeoJSON for points.
