Creates a multidimensional array of LatLngs from a GeoJSON coordinates array. levelsDeep specifies the nesting level (0 is for an array of points, 1 for an array of arrays of points, etc., 0 by default). Can use a custom coordsToLatLng function.

latLngToCoords(latlng: LatLngExpression, precision?: number | false)number[]

Reverse of coordsToLatLng. Coordinates values are rounded with formatNum function.

latLngsToCoords(latlngs: any[], levelsDeep?: number, close?: boolean, precision?: number | false)any[]

Reverse of coordsToLatLngs. close determines whether the first point should be appended to the end of the array to close the feature, only used when levelsDeep is 0. False by default. Coordinates values are rounded with formatNum function.

getFeature(layer: Layer, newGeometry: Geometry)Feature

Returns GeoJSON geometries/features of layer with new GeoJSON geometry.

asFeature(geojson: GeoJsonObject)Feature | FeatureCollection

Normalize GeoJSON geometries/features into GeoJSON features.

Classification

Classifies features by the value of an attribute, for thematic maps: each class has a symbol (path options such as fillColor) and a legend label. A class is either given by value ({value: 'S2'}, or several values sharing one class {value: ['S1', 'S2']}) or by range ({lower: 0, upper: 10} for 0 ≤ value < 10, either bound left out for an open end); both kinds may be mixed in one classification. A feature is classified by its exact value first, then by range, then by legend label, else it falls into the otherValues class.

Use style as style option of GeoJSON to style the features by their class, and LegendControl.addClassification() to show the classes in a legend, with the feature count per class.

Usage example

const temperature = new Classification([
	{value: null, symbol: {fillColor: '#000000'}, legend: 'No data', counted: false},
	{upper: 0, symbol: {fillColor: '#5bc0de'}, legend: '< 0 °C'},
	{lower: 0, upper: 10, symbol: {fillColor: '#33ee33'}, legend: '0–10 °C'},
	{lower: 10, symbol: {fillColor: '#f0a030'}, legend: '≥ 10 °C'}
], {name: 'Air temperature', value: 'temperature'});

const stations = new GeoJSON(data, {
	pointToLayer: (feature, latlng) => new CircleMarker(latlng, {color: '#ffffff'}),
	style: temperature.style
}).addTo(map);

temperature.classify(data.features[0]).legend; // e.g. '0–10 °C'

Inspired by the categorized and graduated renderers of QGIS.

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new Classification(classes: ClassificationClass[], options?: ClassificationOptions)

Creates a classification from the given classes. Each class is an object with value (a value or an array of values) or lower/upper (a range including lower, excluding upper), a symbol (path options), a legend label, and counted: false to exclude the class from the feature count (e.g. "no data").

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
namestring''

The name of the classification, shown as title of its legend.

valuestring|((feature: any) => any)

The value to classify by: the name of a property of the feature, or a function receiving the feature and returning the value. Without it, the argument of classify() is the value itself.

normalize(value: any) => any

A function applied to the values of the classes and of the features before comparing them, for tolerant matching, e.g. v => String(v).trim().toUpperCase().

otherValuesClassificationClass

The class of all values not matching any other class, with symbol and legend (default "All other values"). Without it, such features are not classified.

Methods

MethodReturnsDescription
style(feature: any)PathOptions

Returns the symbol of the class of the feature (an empty object for features without class), bound to the classification for the style option of GeoJSON.

feature
A Feature, a Layer with a feature, or a value.
classify(feature: any)ClassificationClass | undefined

Returns the class of the given GeoJSON feature, of a layer with a feature (as created by GeoJSON) or, without the value option, of a value: one of the classes passed to the constructor, the otherValues class or undefined.

feature
A Feature, a Layer with a feature, or a value.
legendItems()ClassificationLegendItem[]

Returns the items of the legend, {legend, symbol, counted, classes}, in the order of the classes and otherValues last. Classes with the same legend label and symbol share one item.

featureCount(features: any[])ClassificationFeatureCount[]

Counts the given features (or layers with a feature) per legend item, returning the legend items with count and share (the fraction of the counted features). Classes with counted: false get a count, but no share, and do not count toward the total.

Features, Layers with a feature, or values.

Static members

MethodReturnsDescription
quantile(values: number[], n: number){ lower?: number; upper?: number; }[]

Returns n ranges {lower, upper} with about the same number of the given values each (fewer for repeated values), the first and last range open-ended. Add a symbol (and a legend) to each to create a Classification.

equalInterval(values: number[], n: number){ lower?: number; upper?: number; }[]

Returns n ranges {lower, upper} of equal width between the minimum and the maximum of the given values, the first and last range open-ended.

GridLayer extends Layer

Generic class for handling a tiled grid of HTML elements. This is the base class for all tile layers and replaces TileLayer.Canvas. GridLayer can be extended to create a tiled grid of HTML elements like <canvas>, <img> or <div>. GridLayer will handle creating and animating these DOM elements for you.

Layers extending GridLayer shall reimplement the createTile() method.

Usage example

Synchronous usage

To create a custom layer, extend GridLayer and implement the createTile() method, which will be passed a Point object with the x, y, and z (zoom level) coordinates to draw your tile.

class CanvasLayer extends GridLayer {
    createTile(coords) {
        // create a <canvas> element for drawing
        const tile = DomUtil.create('canvas', 'maplair-tile');

        // setup tile width and height according to the options
        const size = this.getTileSize();
        tile.width = size.x;
        tile.height = size.y;

        // get a canvas context and draw something on it using coords.x, coords.y and coords.z
        const ctx = tile.getContext('2d');

        // return the tile so it can be rendered on screen
        return tile;
    }
}

Asynchronous usage

Tile creation can also be asynchronous, this is useful when using a third-party drawing library. Once the tile is finished drawing it can be passed to the done() callback.

class CanvasLayer extends GridLayer {
    createTile(coords, done) {
        const error;

        // create a <canvas> element for drawing
        const tile = DomUtil.create('canvas', 'maplair-tile');

        // setup tile width and height according to the options
        const size = this.getTileSize();
        tile.width = size.x;
        tile.height = size.y;

        // draw something asynchronously and pass the tile to the done() callback
        setTimeout(function() {
            done(error, tile);
        }, 1000);

        return tile;
    }
}

Creates a new instance of GridLayer with the supplied options.

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
tileSizenumber|Point256

Width and height of tiles in the grid. Use a number if width and height are equal, or Point(width, height) otherwise.

opacitynumber1

Opacity of the tiles. Can be used in the createTile() function.

placeholderstring|nullnull

A CSS background shown in place of tiles while they are loading, e.g. '#ddd' or 'url(loading.svg) center no-repeat #eee'. Tiles with a placeholder appear without fading in.

updateWhenIdlebooleanfalse

Load new tiles only when panning ends.

updateWhenZoomingbooleantrue

By default, a smooth zoom animation (during a pinch zoom or a flyTo()) will update grid layers every integer zoom level. Setting this option to false will update the grid layer only when the smooth animation ends.

updateIntervalnumber200

Tiles will not update more than once every updateInterval milliseconds when panning.

zIndexnumber1

The explicit zIndex of the tile layer.

boundsLatLngBoundsExpression|nullnull

If set, tiles will only be loaded inside the set LatLngBounds.

minZoomnumber0

The minimum zoom level down to which this layer will be displayed (inclusive).

maxZoomnumber

The maximum zoom level up to which this layer will be displayed (inclusive).

maxNativeZoomnumber

Maximum zoom number the tile source has available. If it is specified, the tiles on all zoom levels higher than maxNativeZoom will be loaded from maxNativeZoom level and auto-scaled.

minNativeZoomnumber

Minimum zoom number the tile source has available. If it is specified, the tiles on all zoom levels lower than minNativeZoom will be loaded from minNativeZoom level and auto-scaled.

noWrapbooleanfalse

Whether the layer is wrapped around the antimeridian. If true, the GridLayer will only be displayed once at low zoom levels. Has no effect when the map CRS doesn't wrap around. Can be used in combination with bounds to prevent requesting tiles outside the CRS limits.

panestring'tilePane'

Map pane where the grid layer will be added.

classNamestring''

A custom class name to assign to the tile layer. Empty by default.

pixelatedbooleanfalse

Whether to scale the tiles with nearest-neighbour interpolation (image-rendering: pixelated) instead of smoothing them, so that their pixels stay crisp, e.g. while zooming or beyond maxNativeZoom. Useful for raster data, pixel art or scientific imagery.

keepBuffernumber2

When panning the map, keep this many rows and columns of tiles before unloading them.

By default the layer will be added to the map's overlay pane (overlayPane). Overriding this option will cause the layer to be placed on another pane by default. Not effective if the renderer option is set (the renderer option will override the pane option).

String to be shown in the attribution control, e.g. "© OpenStreetMap contributors". It describes the layer data and is often a legal obligation towards copyright holders and tile providers.

The position of the attribution in the attribution control: attributions are sorted by it, then by the order of adding, e.g. 1 keeps a legend last.

LatLng

Represents a geographical point with a certain latitude and longitude.

Usage example

const latlng = new LatLng(50.5, 30.5);

All Maplair methods that accept LatLng objects also accept them in a simple Array form and simple object form (unless noted otherwise), so these lines are equivalent:

map.panTo([50, 30]);
map.panTo({lat: 50, lng: 30});
map.panTo({lat: 50, lon: 30});
map.panTo(new LatLng(50, 30));

Note that LatLng does not inherit from Maplair's Class object, which means new classes can't inherit from it, and new methods can't be added to it with the include function.

Creates an object representing a geographical point with the given latitude and longitude (and optionally altitude). Alternatively, expects a LatLng object, an array of the form [lat, lng] or [lat, lng, alt], or a plain object of the form {lat, lng} or {lat, lng, alt} (lon can be used in place of lng) instead.

Latitude in degrees, or the coordinates.
lng
Longitude in degrees.
alt
Altitude in meters.

Parses coordinates in decimal degrees: a pair of numbers (latitude first), e.g. '47.27, 11.4' or '47.27 11.4', with the hemispheres before or after the numbers, e.g. 'N 47.27, E 11.4', '47.27° S 11.4° W' (also longitude first), or a geo URI like 'geo:47.27,11.4' (with an optional altitude). Returns null for other text and out-of-range coordinates.

LatLng.parse('47.2692 N, 11.4041 E'); // LatLng(47.2692, 11.4041)
LatLng.parse('geo:47.2692,11.4041?z=13'); // LatLng(47.2692, 11.4041)

LatLngBounds

Represents a rectangular geographical area on a map.

Usage example

const corner1 = new LatLng(40.712, -74.227),
corner2 = new LatLng(40.774, -74.125),
bounds = new LatLngBounds(corner1, corner2);

All Maplair methods that accept LatLngBounds objects also accept them in a simple Array form (unless noted otherwise), so the bounds example above can be passed like this:

map.fitBounds([
	[40.712, -74.227],
	[40.774, -74.125]
]);

Caution: if the area crosses the antimeridian (often confused with the International Date Line), you must specify corners outside the [-180, 180] degrees longitude range.

Note that LatLngBounds does not inherit from Maplair's Class object, which means new classes can't inherit from it, and new methods can't be added to it with the include function.

Icon extends Class

Represents an icon to provide when creating a marker.

DefaultIcon extends Icon and is the blue icon Maplair uses for markers by default.

Usage example

const myIcon = new Icon({
    iconUrl: 'my-icon.png',
    iconRetinaUrl: 'my-icon@2x.png',
    iconSize: [38, 95],
    iconAnchor: [22, 94],
    popupAnchor: [-3, -76],
    shadowUrl: 'my-icon-shadow.png',
    shadowRetinaUrl: 'my-icon-shadow@2x.png',
    shadowSize: [68, 95],
    shadowAnchor: [22, 94]
});

new Marker([50.505, 30.57], {icon: myIcon}).addTo(map);

DefaultIcon extends Icon

A trivial subclass of Icon, represents the icon to use in Markers when no icon is specified. The maple leaf marker and its shadow are inlined as SVG data URIs, so they work with any bundler and need no image files.

In order to customize the default icon, just change the properties of DefaultIcon.defaultOptions (which is a set of Icon options).

If you want to completely replace the default icon, override the Marker.defaultOptions.icon with your own icon instead.

DivIcon extends Icon

Represents a lightweight icon for markers that uses a simple <div> element instead of an image. Inherits from Icon but ignores the iconUrl and shadow options.

SvgIcon extends DefaultIcon

A marker icon in the shape of the default marker (with its shadow), drawn as inline SVG in any color and with an optional glyph – a character, an emoji or an SVG path (e.g. of an icon set) – instead of the white maple leaf. No image per color is needed, and it stays sharp on any screen.

Inspired by the Leaflet.awesome-markers, leaflet-color-markers and Leaflet.ExtraMarkers plugins.

Usage example

new Marker([47.27, 11.40], {icon: new SvgIcon({color: '#2a81cb', glyph: 'P'})}).addTo(map);
new Marker([47.28, 11.41], {icon: new SvgIcon({color: 'green', glyph: '🚲'})}).addTo(map);
// a 24×24 SVG path, e.g. from Material Design Icons
new Marker([47.29, 11.42], {icon: new SvgIcon({color: 'purple', glyphPath: 'M12 2L2 22h20z'})}).addTo(map);

LayersControl extends Control

The layers control gives users the ability to switch between different base layers and switch overlays on/off (check out the detailed example).

Usage example

const baseLayers = {
	"Mapbox": mapbox,
	"OpenStreetMap": osm
};

const overlays = {
	"Marker": marker,
	"Roads": roadsLayer
};

new LayersControl(baseLayers, overlays).addTo(map);

The baseLayers and overlays parameters are object literals with layer names as keys and Layer objects as values:

{
    "<someName1>": layer1,
    "<someName2>": layer2
}

The layer names can contain HTML, which allows you to add additional styling to the items:

{"<img src='my-layer-icon' /> <span class='my-layer-item'>My Layer</span>": myLayer}

Layers can be grouped using the option groupBy, for example layer names of the form "Group (label)":

new LayersControl(baseLayers, overlays, {
	inline: true,
	groupBy(name) {
		const [, group, label] = /^([^<>()]+) \((.+)\)$/.exec(name) ?? [];
		return group ? {group: `${group}:`, label} : undefined;
	}
}).addTo(map);

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new LayersControl(baseLayers?: Record<string, Layer>, overlays?: Record<string, Layer>, options?: LayersControlOptions)

Creates a layers control with the given layers. Base layers will be switched with radio buttons, while overlays will be switched with checkboxes. Note that all base layers should be passed in the base layers object, but only one should be added to the map during map instantiation.

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
collapsedbooleantrue

If true, the control will be collapsed into an icon and expanded on pointer hover, touch, or keyboard activation. Ignored if inline is true.

inlinebooleanfalse

If true, the control is laid out like the attribution control: it is always expanded (without toggle button) and all entries are placed next to each other, wrapping onto multiple lines if necessary.

groupBy(name: string, layer: Layer, overlay: boolean) => LayersControlGroup | undefined

A function to group the entries. For each entry, it returns the name of its group and its label within the group, or undefined for an ungrouped entry. Consecutive entries of the same group (base layers and overlays separately) are rendered within one maplair-control-layers-group container, starting with the group name in a maplair-control-layers-group-name element, and each entry shows only its label. Events like baselayerchange still carry the full name. When combined with sortLayers, the entries are sorted first and grouped afterwards.

toggleContentstring|HTMLElement

The content of the toggle button of a collapsed control instead of the layers icon: HTML (e.g. an icon or a character) or an element. String content is rendered as HTML; do not pass untrusted input.

collapseDelaynumber0

Collapse delay in milliseconds. If greater than 0, the control will remain open longer, making it easier to scroll through long layer lists.

positionstring'topright'

The position of the control (one of the map corners). Possible values are 'topleft', 'topright', 'bottomleft' or 'bottomright'.

autoZIndexbooleantrue

If true, the control will assign zIndexes in increasing order to all of its layers so that the order is preserved when switching them on/off.

hideSingleBasebooleanfalse

If true, the base layers in the control will be hidden when there is only one.

sortLayersbooleanfalse

Whether to sort the layers. When false, layers will keep the order in which they were added to the control.

sortFunction(layerA: Layer, layerB: Layer, nameA: string, nameB: string) => number

A compare function that will be used for sorting the layers, when sortLayers is true. The function receives both the Layer instances and their names, as in sortFunction(layerA, layerB, nameA, nameB). By default, it sorts layers alphabetically by their name.

Options inherited from Control

positionstring'topright'

The position of the control (one of the map corners). Possible values are 'topleft', 'topright', 'bottomleft' or 'bottomright'.

ordernumber0

The position of the control within its corner: controls with a lower order are closer to the corner of the map, those with the same order in the order of adding.

MiniMapControl extends Control

An overview map in a corner of the map, showing the view of the map as a rectangle (or rotated rectangle on a rotated map) at a smaller zoom level. Dragging the overview map pans the map, clicking it centers the map there, and a button collapses it.

Inspired by the Leaflet-MiniMap plugin.

Usage example

// a layer of its own, a layer can only be on one map
const overviewLayer = new TileLayer('https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png');
new MiniMapControl(overviewLayer).addTo(map);

SearchControl extends Control

A control with a search field for places, showing the results in a list to select one with the pointer or the keyboard. The selected result is shown on the map with a marker. It searches with a geocoder, e.g. Nominatim of OpenStreetMap or any other service. Coordinates like 47.27, 11.4 or geo:47.27,11.4 are found without a service.

The public Nominatim service is free, but limited by its usage policy: it is for occasional searches of users, not for heavy use (an absolute maximum of one request per second for all users of an app), and forbids auto-complete. The Nominatim geocoder follows the technical requirements, but you are responsible for your use of the service, which you confirm with the acceptUsagePolicy option: for more traffic, use your own Nominatim server or a commercial provider.

Usage example

new SearchControl({
    geocoder: SearchControl.nominatim({acceptUsagePolicy: true})
}).addTo(map);

// Photon of Komoot, which allows auto-complete
new SearchControl({
    autoComplete: true,
    async geocoder(query, {signal}) {
        const response = await fetch(`https://photon.komoot.io/api/?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`, {signal});
        const {features} = await response.json();
        return features.map(({geometry, properties}) => ({
            label: [properties.name, properties.city, properties.country].filter(Boolean).join(', '),
            latlng: [geometry.coordinates[1], geometry.coordinates[0]],
            raw: properties
        }));
    }
}).addTo(map);

Static members

MethodReturnsDescription
nominatim({ url, params, acceptUsagePolicy }?: { url?: string | undefined; params?: Record<string, string> | undefined; acceptUsagePolicy?: boolean | undefined; })Geocoder

Returns a geocoder searching with Nominatim, by default the public service of OpenStreetMap. Using it requires that you read and accept its usage policy with the acceptUsagePolicy option, otherwise this throws an error. The geocoder sends at most one request per second, caches the results of the last 100 queries, adds the OpenStreetMap attribution to the map and does not search while typing with the public service. For more traffic, use your own Nominatim server or a commercial provider.

new SearchControl({
    geocoder: SearchControl.nominatim({acceptUsagePolicy: true, params: {countrycodes: 'at,de'}})
}).addTo(map);
layers(group: LayerGroup, { property, label, limit }?: { property?: string | undefined; label?: ((layer: Layer) => string | number | null | undefined) | undefined; limit?: number | undefined; })Geocoder

Returns a geocoder searching the layers of a layer group, e.g. the markers of a FeatureGroup or the features of a GeoJSON layer, by their label: a property of their GeoJSON feature (layer.feature.properties) or the result of a function. The group is searched at the time of the search, so layers added later are found as well, and nested groups without a label are searched recursively. The search ignores the case and finds the query anywhere in the label; labels starting with it come first, then in alphabetical order. The results contain the found layer and its GeoJSON feature as raw; layers without a single position (e.g. polygons) have the bounds and their center as latlng. Combine it with autoComplete to search while typing, and with marker false or a function to not cover the found marker with another one.

group
The layer group to search.
const stations = new GeoJSON(data, {
    onEachFeature: (feature, layer) => layer.bindTooltip(feature.properties.name)
}).addTo(map);
new SearchControl({
    geocoder: SearchControl.layers(stations, {property: 'name'}),
    autoComplete: true,
    minLength: 1,
    marker: false
}).addTo(map);
map.on('searchresult', ({result}) => result.layer.openTooltip());

SideBySideControl extends Control

Compares layers side by side: a vertical divider across the map shows the "left" layers on its left and the "right" layers on its right side. The divider can be dragged, or moved with the arrow keys. Works with layers having a container or element of their own, e.g. tile layers and image overlays.

Inspired by the leaflet-side-by-side plugin.

Usage example

const before = new TileLayer('https://…/2020/{z}/{x}/{y}.png').addTo(map);
const after = new TileLayer('https://…/2025/{z}/{x}/{y}.png').addTo(map);
new SideBySideControl(before, after).addTo(map);

ButtonControl extends Control

A control with a button, styled like the zoom control, calling a function when clicked. It can have several states with their own content, title and function, e.g. to toggle something. Several buttons can be grouped with ButtonBarControl.

Inspired by the Leaflet.EasyButton plugin.

Usage example

new ButtonControl({
	content: '⌂',
	title: 'Home',
	onClick: (e, button, map) => map.setView([47.27, 11.40], 13)
}).addTo(map);

new ButtonControl({
	states: [{
		name: 'show',
		content: '👁',
		title: 'Show the markers',
		onClick(e, button, map) { markers.addTo(map); button.setState('hide'); }
	}, {
		name: 'hide',
		content: '🙈',
		title: 'Hide the markers',
		onClick(e, button) { markers.remove(); button.setState('show'); }
	}]
}).addTo(map);

ContextMenu extends Class

A menu opened with the contextmenu event (right click, or long tap on touch screens) on the map or on a layer. Each item calls a function with the location of the event. The menu is a popover, closed by clicking outside of it or pressing Escape, and can be used with the keyboard (arrow keys, Enter).

Inspired by the Leaflet.contextmenu plugin.

Usage example

new ContextMenu([
	{text: 'Center the map here', callback: e => map.panTo(e.latlng)},
	'-',
	{text: 'Zoom in', callback: () => map.zoomIn()}
]).addTo(map);

new ContextMenu([
	{text: 'Remove', callback: e => e.relatedTarget.remove()}
]).addTo(marker);

DisplaceHandler extends Handler

Cartographic displacement of overlapping CircleMarkers: keeps all circle markers created with displace: true free of overlap.

Overlap is a screen space phenomenon: whether two markers cover each other depends on their pixel radius and the current zoom level. The displacement is therefore computed in projected pixel space and recomputed on every zoom. The true position of each marker is kept by the handler, the displaced position is applied via setLatLng. Since every run starts over from the true position, markers never drift.

maxDistance bounds how far a marker may be moved away from the truth, in meters. It is worth noting what such a limit costs at low zoom levels: if a marker is 11 km wide on the ground, separating two coincident ones moves each of them by some 6 km, so a limit below that leaves them overlapping.

Unlike the default handlers, it isn't added to every map, so that bundlers can drop it from applications that don't use it. Add it to the map class (or to a single map with DisplaceHandler.addTo(map, 'displace')), then enable it with the map option displace, which is either true or an object overriding the handler's options. It can be toggled at runtime via map.displace.enable() / map.displace.disable(); disabling restores the true positions.

Usage example

import { CircleMarker, DisplaceHandler, MaplairMap } from 'maplair';

MaplairMap.addInitHook('addHandler', 'displace', DisplaceHandler);

const map = new MaplairMap('map', {displace: { maxDistance: 10_000} });
new CircleMarker(latlng, { displace: true, radius: 6 }).addTo(map);

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new DisplaceHandler(map: MaplairMap)

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
gapnumber2

Additional pixel distance between the outlines of two markers.

iterationsnumber80

Maximum number of relaxation passes per relayout.

maxDistancenumberInfinity

Maximum distance in meters a marker may be moved away from its true position. Markers which would have to move further stay overlapping. Meters rather than pixels, since the point of the limit is to bound the geographic error. A limit in meters also scales itself: it only bites at the zoom levels where a pixel is worth a lot of ground.

Transformation

Represents an affine transformation: a set of coefficients a, b, c, d for transforming a point of a form (x, y) into (a*x + b, c*y + d) and doing the reverse. Used by Maplair in its projections code.

Usage example

const transformation = new Transformation(2, 5, -1, 10),
	p = new Point(1, 2),
	p2 = transformation.transform(p), //  new Point(7, 8)
	p3 = transformation.untransform(p2); //  new Point(1, 2)

Dramatically reduces the number of points in a polyline while retaining its shape and returns a new array of simplified points, using the Ramer-Douglas-Peucker algorithm. Used for a huge performance boost when processing/displaying Maplair polylines for each zoom level and also reducing visual noise. tolerance affects the amount of simplification (lesser value means higher quality but slower and with more points). MethodReturnsDescription
callInitHooks(cls?: Function)this

Runs the constructor hooks of the given class and of its parent classes, which haven't run yet for this object. Classes call it at the end of their constructor, e.g. this.callInitHooks(MyClass). Without cls, runs the hooks of all classes of this object.

Class

Class powers the OOP facilities of Maplair and is used to create almost all of the Maplair classes documented here.

It implements a simple classical inheritance model using JavaScript's standard extends keyword, and introduces several special properties for convenient code organization — options and init hooks.

Options

options is a special property whose defaults, the static defaultOptions of the class, are merged with those of the parent class instead of overriding them completely, which makes managing configuration of objects and default values convenient:

class MyClass extends Class {
    static defaultOptions = {
        myOption1: 'foo',
        myOption2: 'bar'
    };
}

class MyChildClass extends MyClass {
    static defaultOptions = {
        myOption1: 'baz',
        myOption3: 5
    };
}

const a = new MyChildClass();
a.options.myOption1; // 'baz'
a.options.myOption2; // 'bar'
a.options.myOption3; // 5

There's also Util.setOptions, a method for conveniently merging options passed to constructor with the defaults defined in the class:

class MyClass extends Class {
    static defaultOptions = {
        foo: 'bar',
        bla: 5
    };

    constructor(options) {
        super();
        Util.setOptions(this, options);
        ...
    }
}

const a = new MyClass({bla: 10});
a.options; // {foo: 'bar', bla: 10}

Note that the options object allows any keys, not just the options defined by the class and its base classes. This means you can use the options object to store application specific information, as long as you avoid keys that are already used by the class in question.

Mixins

You can add methods and properties from other objects using the include method (such objects are called mixins):

const MyMixin = {
    foo() { ... },
    bar: 5
};

class MyClass extends Class {}

MyClass.include(MyMixin);

const a = new MyClass();
a.foo();

Constructor hooks

If you're a plugin developer, you often need to add additional initialization code to existing classes (e.g. editing hooks for Polyline). Maplair comes with a way to do it easily using the addInitHook method:

Polyline.addInitHook(function () {
    // ... do something in constructor additionally
    // e.g. add event listeners, set custom properties etc.
    this.editing = new PolylineEditor(this);
});

You can also use the following shortcut when you just need to make one additional method call:

MyClass.addInitHook('methodName', arg1, arg2, …);

The hooks of a class run at the end of its constructor, which calls callInitHooks — so they can rely on everything the constructor sets up. All Maplair classes do so. Hooks of parent classes run first, and parent classes without a constructor of their own (such as Layer or Path) have their hooks run along with their subclasses. Each hook runs once per object.

Note that the hooks of a parent class run before the constructor of a subclass continues. To support hooks on your own classes, call this.callInitHooks() at the end of their constructor:

class MyMarker extends Marker {
    constructor(latlng, options) {
        super(latlng, options); // runs the hooks of Marker (and of Layer etc.)
        this.extra = 'ready';
        this.callInitHooks();   // runs the hooks of MyMarker
    }
}

Usage example

class MyClass extends Class {
    constructor(greeter) {
        super();
        this.greeter = greeter;
        this.callInitHooks(MyClass); // optional, see constructor hooks above
    }

    greet(name) {
        alert(this.greeter + ', ' + name)
    }
}

// create instance of MyClass, passing "Hello" to the constructor
const a = new MyClass("Hello");

// call greet method, alerting "Hello, World"
a.greet("World");

Evented extends Class

A set of methods shared between event-powered classes (like Map and Marker). Generally, events allow you to execute some function when something happens with an object (e.g. the user clicks on the map, causing the map to fire 'click' event).

Usage example

map.on('click', function(e) {
	alert(e.latlng);
} );

Maplair deals with event listeners by reference, so if you want to add a listener and then remove it, define it as a function:

function onClick(e) { ... }

map.on('click', onClick);
map.off('click', onClick);

Layer extends Evented

The base class of all Maplair layers, with the methods they share.

Every layer should extend from Layer and (re-)implement the following methods:

  • onAdd(map: MaplairMap): this should contain code that creates DOM elements for the layer, adds them to map panes where they should belong and puts listeners on relevant map events. Called on map.addLayer(layer).
  • onRemove(map: MaplairMap): this should contain all clean up code that removes the layer's elements from the DOM and removes listeners previously added in onAdd. Called on map.removeLayer(layer).
  • getEvents(): Object (optional) should return an object like { viewreset: this._reset } for on. The event handlers in this object will be automatically added and removed from the map with your layer.
  • getAttribution(): String (optional) should return a string containing HTML to be shown on the Attribution control whenever the layer is visible.
  • getLegend(): HTMLElement|String (optional) should return an element (or a string containing HTML) to be shown on the LegendControl whenever the layer is visible. Fire legendchange on the layer when the legend changes.
  • beforeAdd(map: MaplairMap): this (optional) is called on map.addLayer(layer), before the layer is added to the map, before events are initialized, without waiting until the map is in a usable state. Use for early initialization only.

Usage example

const layer = new Marker(latlng).addTo(map);
layer.addTo(map);
layer.remove();

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
panestring'overlayPane'

By default the layer will be added to the map's overlay pane (overlayPane). Overriding this option will cause the layer to be placed on another pane by default. Not effective if the renderer option is set (the renderer option will override the pane option).

attributionstring|nullnull

String to be shown in the attribution control, e.g. "© OpenStreetMap contributors". It describes the layer data and is often a legal obligation towards copyright holders and tile providers.

attributionOrdernumber0

The position of the attribution in the attribution control: attributions are sorted by it, then by the order of adding, e.g. 1 keeps a legend last.

pointerdownMaplairPointerEventFired when the user pushes the pointer on the layer, if it is interactive.
pointerupMaplairPointerEventFired when the user releases the pointer pushed on the layer, if it is interactive.
pointeroverMaplairPointerEventFired when the pointer enters the layer, if it is interactive.
pointeroutMaplairPointerEventFired when the pointer leaves the layer, if it is interactive.
contextmenuMaplairPointerEventFired when the user right-clicks on the layer, if it is interactive; prevents default browser context menu from showing if there are listeners on this event. Also fired on mobile when the user holds a single touch for a second (also called long press).
popupopenPopupEventFired when a popup bound to this layer is opened.
popupclosePopupEventFired when a popup bound to this layer is closed.

Control extends Class

Control is a base class for implementing map controls. Handles positioning. All other controls extend from this class.

Every control should extend from Control and (re-)implement the following methods:

  • onAdd(map: MaplairMap): HTMLElement should return the container DOM element for the control and add listeners on relevant map events. Called on control.addTo(map).
  • onRemove(map: MaplairMap) (optional) should contain all clean up code that removes the listeners previously added in onAdd. Called on control.remove().

The position of the control (one of the map corners). Possible values are 'topleft', 'topright', 'bottomleft' or 'bottomright'.

ordernumber0

The position of the control within its corner: controls with a lower order are closer to the corner of the map, those with the same order in the order of adding.

BlanketOverlay extends Layer

Represents an HTML element that covers ("blankets") the entire surface of the map.

Do not use this class directly. It's meant for Renderer, and for plugins that rely on one single HTML element.

Subclasses must define the following methods:

  • _initContainer() must initialize the HTML element to use as blanket, and store it as this._container. The base implementation creates a blank <div>.
  • _destroyContainer() must destroy the HTML element in this._container and free any other resources. The base implementation destroys the element and removes any event handlers attached to it.
  • _resizeContainer(): Point: the base implementation resizes the container (based on the map's size and taking into account the padding), returning the new size in CSS pixels. Subclass implementations shall reset container parameters and data structures as needed.
  • _onZoomEnd(ev?: PointerEvent) (optional) runs on the map's zoomend event.
  • _onViewReset(ev?: PointerEvent) (optional) runs on the map's viewreset event.
  • _onSettled() runs whenever the map state settles after changing (at the end of pan/zoom animations, etc). This should trigger the bulk of any rendering logic. If the continuous option is set to true, then this also runs on any map state change (including during pan/zoom animations).

Constructor

ConstructorDescription
new BlanketOverlay(options?: BlanketOverlayOptions)

Options

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
paddingnumber0.1

How much to extend the clip area around the map view (relative to its size) e.g. 0.1 would be 10% of map view in each direction.

continuousbooleanfalse

When false, the blanket will update its position only when the map state settles (after a pan/zoom animation). When true, it will update when the map state changes (during pan/zoom animations).

Renderer extends BlanketOverlay

Base class for vector renderer implementations (SVG, Canvas). Handles the DOM container of the renderer, its bounds, and its zoom animation.

A Renderer works as an implicit layer group for all Paths - the renderer itself can be added or removed to the map. All paths use a renderer, which can be implicit (the map will decide the type of renderer and use it automatically) or explicit (using the renderer option of the path).

Do not use this class directly, use SVG and Canvas instead.

The continuous option inherited from BlanketOverlay cannot be set to true (otherwise, renderers get out of place during a pinch-zoom operation).

Methods inherited from Evented
MethodReturnsDescription
on(types: string | Record<string, EventListener>, fn?: EventListener | object, context?: object)this

Adds a listener function (fn) to a particular event type of the object. You can optionally specify the context of the listener (object the this keyword will point to). You can also pass several space-separated types (e.g. 'click dblclick'). Alternatively, adds a set of type/listener pairs, e.g. {click: onClick, pointermove: onPointerMove}, with the context as second argument.

off(types?: string | Record<string, EventListener>, fn?: EventListener | object, context?: object, …args: any[])this

Removes a previously added listener function. If no function is specified, it will remove all the listeners of that particular event from the object. Note that if you passed a custom context to on, you must pass the same context to off in order to remove the listener. Alternatively, removes a set of type/listener pairs. Without arguments, removes all listeners to all events on the object, including implicitly attached events.

fire(type: string, data?: object, propagate?: boolean)this

Fires an event of the specified type. You can optionally provide a data object — the first argument of the listener function will contain its properties. The event can optionally be propagated to event parents.

listens(type: string, fn?: EventListener | boolean, context?: object, propagate?: boolean)boolean

Returns true if a particular event type has any listeners attached to it (or the given listener function, with the given context). The verification can optionally be propagated, it will return true if parents have the listener attached to it. Called as listens(type, propagate?) or listens(type, fn, context?, propagate?).

once(types: string | Record<string, EventListener>, fn?: EventListener | object, context?: object)this

Behaves as on(…), except the listener will only get fired once and then removed.

addEventParent(obj: Evented)this

Adds an event parent - an Evented that will receive propagated events.

removeEventParent(obj: Evented)this

Removes an event parent, so it will stop receiving propagated events.

Runs the constructor hooks of the given class and of its parent classes, which haven't run yet for this object. Classes call it at the end of their constructor, e.g. this.callInitHooks(MyClass). Without cls, runs the hooks of all classes of this object.

CRS

Object that defines coordinate reference systems for projecting geographical points into pixel (screen) coordinates and back (and to coordinates in other units for WMS services). See spatial reference system.

Maplair defines the most usual CRSs by default. If you want to use a CRS not defined by default, extend CRS with a projection of your own, e.g. based on Proj4js (the Leaflet plugin Proj4Leaflet doesn't work with Maplair).

The CRSs are classes with static properties and methods only; they are not instantiated, the class itself is passed as the CRS, e.g. to the crs option of the map. Maplair's CRSs extend CRS (EarthCRS for the global ones).

Besides the properties and methods below, a CRS may define:

  • code: string: Standard code name of the CRS passed into WMS services (e.g. 'EPSG:3857').
  • wrapLng: [number, number]: An array of two numbers defining whether the longitude (horizontal) coordinate axis wraps around a given range and how. Defaults to [-180, 180] in most geographical CRSs. If undefined, the longitude axis does not wrap around.
  • wrapLat: [number, number]: Like wrapLng, but for the latitude (vertical) axis.
  • distance(latlng1: LatLng, latlng2: LatLng): number: Returns the distance between two geographical coordinates.

Static members

MethodReturnsDescription
latLngToPoint(latlng: LatLngExpression, zoom: number)Point

Projects geographical coordinates into pixel coordinates for a given zoom.

pointToLatLng(point: Point, zoom: number)LatLng

The inverse of latLngToPoint. Projects pixel coordinates on a given zoom into geographical coordinates.

project(latlng: LatLngExpression)Point

Projects geographical coordinates into coordinates in units accepted for this CRS (e.g. meters for EPSG:3857, for passing it to WMS services).

unproject(point: Point)LatLng

Given a projected coordinate returns the corresponding LatLng. The inverse of project.

scale(zoom: number)number

Returns the scale used when transforming projected coordinates into pixel coordinates for a particular zoom. For example, it returns 256 * 2^zoom for Mercator-based CRS.

zoom(scale: number)number

Inverse of scale(), returns the zoom level corresponding to a scale factor of scale.

getProjectedBounds(zoom: number)Bounds | null

Returns the projection's bounds scaled and transformed for the provided zoom (null if the CRS is infinite).

wrapLatLng(latlng: LatLngExpression)LatLng

Returns a LatLng where lat and lng has been wrapped according to the CRS's wrapLat and wrapLng properties, if they are outside the CRS's bounds.

wrapLatLngBounds(bounds: LatLngBoundsExpression)LatLngBounds

Returns a LatLngBounds with the same size as the given one, ensuring that its center is within the CRS's bounds.

PropertyTypeDescription
projectionProjection | undefined

The projection of the CRS.

transformationTransformation | undefined

The transformation of projected coordinates into pixel coordinates at zoom 0.

infiniteboolean

If true, the coordinate space will be unbounded (infinite in both axes).

EarthCRS extends CRS

Serves as the base for CRS that are global such that they cover the earth. Can only be used as the base for other CRS and cannot be used directly, since it does not have a code, projection or transformation. distance() returns meters.

Rnumber

Mean Earth Radius in meters, as recommended for use by the International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics, see https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Haversine_formula

EPSG3857 extends EarthCRS

The most common CRS for online maps, used by almost all free and commercial tile providers. Uses Spherical Mercator projection. Set in by default in Map's crs option.

EPSG4326 extends EarthCRS

A common CRS among GIS enthusiasts. Uses simple Equirectangular projection.

Maplair complies with the TMS coordinate scheme for EPSG:4326. If you are using a TileLayer with this CRS, ensure that there are two 256x256 pixel tiles covering the whole earth at zoom level zero, and that the tile coordinate origin is (-180,+90), or (-180,-90) for TileLayers with the tms option set.

SimpleCRS extends CRS

A simple CRS that maps longitude and latitude into x and y directly. May be used for maps of flat surfaces (e.g. game maps). Note that the y axis should still be inverted (going from bottom to top). distance() returns simple euclidean distance.

MaplairEvent

The base event object, the argument of event listeners. All other event objects contain these properties too. Whenever a class inheriting from Evented fires an event, a listener function is called with an event object containing information about the event, which depends on the event type. For example:

map.on('click', function(ev) {
    alert(ev.latlng); // ev is an event object (MaplairPointerEvent in this case)
});

Properties

PropertyTypeDescription
typestring

The event type (e.g. 'click').

targetany

The object that fired the event. For propagated events, the last object in the propagation chain that fired the event.

sourceTargetany

The object that originally fired the event. For non-propagated events, this will be the same as the target.

propagatedFromany

For propagated events, the last object that propagated the event to its event parent.

EventListener

A listener of events, called with the event object, which has more properties depending on the event type (see the event objects below).

LatLngExpression

A geographical point: a LatLng, an array of the form [lat, lng] or [lat, lng, alt], or a plain object of the form {lat, lng} or {lat, lng, alt} (lon can be used in place of lng). Accepted by all Maplair methods which accept LatLng objects (unless noted otherwise). Plain arrays (number[]) are accepted for JavaScript, where array literals in variables are no tuples.

type LatLngExpression = LatLng | [number, number] | [number, number, number] | number[] | { lat: number; lng: number; alt?: number; } | { lat: number; lon: number; alt?: number; }

LatLngBoundsExpression

A geographical area: a LatLngBounds, or an array of geographical points (usually two diagonally opposite corners), e.g. [[40.712, -74.227], [40.774, -74.125]]. Accepted by all Maplair methods which accept LatLngBounds objects (unless noted otherwise).

type LatLngBoundsExpression = LatLngBounds | LatLngExpression[]

PointExpression

A point in pixels: a Point, an array of the form [x, y], or a plain object of the form {x, y}. Accepted by all Maplair methods and options which accept Point objects (unless noted otherwise).

type PointExpression = Point | [number, number] | number[] | { x: number; y: number; }

BoundsExpression

A rectangular area in pixel coordinates: a Bounds, or an array of points (usually two diagonally opposite corners), e.g. [[10, 10], [40, 60]]. Accepted by all Maplair methods which accept Bounds objects (unless noted otherwise).

type BoundsExpression = Bounds | PointExpression[]

ZoomOptions

Options of the MaplairMap methods which modify the zoom level.

Properties

PropertyTypeDescription
animateboolean

If not specified, zoom animation will happen if the zoom origin is inside the current view, and if the user prefers reduced motion, only when zooming by at most one level. If true, the map will attempt animating zoom disregarding where zoom origin is and the user's reduced motion preference. Setting false will make it always reset the view completely without animation.

PanOptions

Options of the MaplairMap methods which modify the center of the map.

Properties

OptionTypeDefaultDescription
animateboolean

If true, panning will always be animated if possible, even if the user prefers reduced motion. If false, it will not animate panning, either resetting the map view if panning more than a screen away, or just setting a new offset for the map pane (except for panBy which always does the latter). If not specified, panning is animated, except for pans longer than half the map size when the user prefers reduced motion.

durationnumber0.25

Duration of animated panning, in seconds.

easeLinearitynumber0.25

The curvature factor of panning animation easing (third parameter of the Cubic Bezier curve). 1.0 means linear animation, and the smaller this number, the more bowed the curve.

noMoveStartbooleanfalse

If true, panning won't fire movestart event on start (used internally for panning inertia).

Equivalent of setting both top left and bottom right padding to the same value.

SearchResult

A result of a search, returned by a geocoder.

Properties

PropertyTypeDescription
labelstring

The text shown in the list of results, e.g. an address.

latlngLatLngExpression

The position of the result.

boundsLatLngBoundsExpression

The extent of the result, e.g. of a city, which the map fits to instead of zooming to the position.

rawany

The original result of the service, for use in event listeners.

layerLayer

The found layer, by SearchControl.layers(), e.g. to open its tooltip in a searchresult listener.

Geocoder

A function searching places for a query, see the geocoder option. It should pass the signal to fetch(): searches are aborted when the user starts another one. Optional properties of the function: attribution, an attribution text which the control adds to the map, and autoComplete: false if the service forbids searching while typing (overriding the autoComplete option).

type Geocoder = ((query: string, options: { signal: AbortSignal; }) => Promise<SearchResult[]>) & { attribution?: string; autoComplete?: boolean; }

version

A constant that represents the Maplair version in use.
